drivers: D010 - Modern Statistical Methods and Methodological Innovation
D011 - Operational Efficiency and Cost Discipline

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected because subprocess 1.1 focuses on investigating what statistics are needed, including triggers such as periodic review, respondent feedback, environmental change and action plans from prior evaluations. The work description directly supports assessment of current and future data requirements and evaluation of relevance and performance. The capability needed is to gather evidence on user and program needs, analyze qualitative and quantitative inputs, and assess cost and value implications. This role satisfies that need through activities such as 'Provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data', 'conducting literature and data research', 'identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data', and 'participating in the conduct of interviews, and focus groups'. It is also strongly aligned to the cost-discipline driver because it includes 'cost-benefit analysis of programs' and evaluation of program relevance and performance. It further supports methodological consideration through recommending 'enhancements to methods for retrieving data' and using research methods to inform study approaches.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is connected because identifying statistical needs includes determining what is needed of the statistics, which often includes metadata, documentation, standards and comparability across programs and organizations. The capability needed is to interpret client requirements, translate them into metadata specifications, and understand statistical program methodologies and standards. This work description satisfies that need through evidence such as 'liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications', 'interprets client requirements in order to determine options for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata', and knowledge of 'statistical metadata concepts and frameworks used within Statistics Canada, the Government of Canada and internationally'. It is also relevant to methodological innovation because it provides feedback on 'current or proposed methods and procedures' and participates in testing new procedures and systems. Relevance is medium because the role is more focused on metadata production and quality than on leading the broader identification and prioritization of statistical needs.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because subprocess 1.1 requires evidence-based identification of information needs, feasibility considerations, and awareness of modern analytical approaches. The capability needed is to organize and analyze data relevant to study objectives, discuss data requirements with stakeholders, and understand evolving methods across the data life cycle. This work description satisfies that need through 'Organizes and consolidates information relevant to the defined objectives of studies', 'Attends Departmental meetings, and interdepartmental and stakeholder meetings (as required), to gather data/information', and communication requirements to 'discuss data requirements with operations managers... clients or service providers' and 'liaise with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications'. It is particularly relevant to driver D010 because it requires knowledge of 'data science and its life cycle' and 'leading edge thinking and methodologies to data analytics', and to D011 through assessing data quality, risks and utility of data assets. Relevance is medium because the role supports needs identification analytically rather than owning program-level prioritization.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is connected because identifying needs includes understanding operational feasibility, respondent issues, and the implications of changes to collection and processing under budget or efficiency pressures. The capability needed is to evaluate collection and coding methods, understand operational conditions, and identify impacts of changes to data sources and outputs. This work description satisfies that need through 'Evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives', 'Meets with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others, in order to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur', and 'Contacts data suppliers or respondents to obtain their collaboration... to clarify problems or irregularities'. It also aligns strongly with D011 because it includes 'Analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results' and prepares 'reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems'. Relevance is medium because the role informs needs identification from an operational and efficiency perspective rather than leading the full needs assessment.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is strongly implicated because subprocess 1.1 requires identifying emerging information needs, reviewing existing programs, considering methodological changes, and assessing feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs. The capability needed is subject-matter analysis, trend identification, translation of user requirements into program specifications, and assessment of methodological and program impacts. This work description satisfies that need through 'Identifies statistical trends and developments', 'participates in subject matter studies and reviews', and communication to 'develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs'. It directly addresses methodological innovation and redesign through knowledge of 'methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling', 'methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs', and research activities that 'analyze current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems'. This is highly aligned to both D010 and D011.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because identifying needs includes interpreting user information requests, assessing feasibility of outputs, and understanding how changes in methods or systems affect products and services. The capability needed is to interpret client demand, assess data quality and feasibility, and provide consultative services on statistical outputs. This work description satisfies that need through 'Interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations', 'Provides statistical data and consultative services to users', and research activities that 'interpret user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required'. It also supports methodological and efficiency drivers through 'Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases' and 'Analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services'. Relevance is medium because the role engages directly with user demand and feasibility, but is more downstream in production and dissemination than primary strategic needs identification.

drivers: D006 - Metadata, Data Standards and Discoverability
D012 - Governance, Prioritization and Execution Discipline

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is directly implicated because subprocess 1.2 requires detailed consultation with stakeholders to confirm not just what statistics are needed, but also how they must be documented, discovered, accessed and delivered. Driver D006 is especially central: the work description explicitly focuses on statistical metadata, standards, dissemination and quality evaluation, which are all part of confirming requirements for searchable, interoperable and reusable data assets. The role requires the capability to interpret client requirements and translate them into metadata specifications, and to advise clients on standards and policies. This satisfies the subprocess need to confirm detailed user requirements around metadata richness and standards-based delivery. Evidence includes: 'provides assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines'; 'liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata'; and 'interprets client requirements in order to determine options for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata.' Driver D012 is also relevant because the role negotiates 'procedural modifications, priorities and target dates,' supporting clearer prioritization and execution discipline when needs compete.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected because consulting and confirming needs includes understanding user information requests, feasibility, delivery options and dissemination expectations. The role directly interprets client requests and provides consultative services to users, which aligns strongly with the subprocess emphasis on confirming what users need, when and how. It also supports D006 because discoverability and reusable delivery requirements often surface through dissemination and custom tabulation requests, and the role works in dissemination, interpretation of requests and adaptation of outputs. It supports D012 through assessing feasibility and translating requirements into specifications, which helps prioritize and operationalize stakeholder needs. Evidence includes: 'Interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations'; 'Provides statistical data and consultative services to users'; 'Liaises with other specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development'; and 'Interprets user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required.' These responsibilities directly satisfy the need for stakeholder consultation, requirement clarification and disciplined confirmation of deliverable options.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because subprocess 1.2 depends on translating stakeholder and subject-matter needs into program specifications and assessing implications for statistical programs. The work description includes liaison with users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements, negotiate modifications, and establish plans, priorities and target dates, which aligns with both confirming needs and D012 governance/prioritization requirements. It is less directly tied to metadata/discoverability than the metadata role, but still relevant where user needs must be converted into program or system changes. Evidence includes: 'Liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates.' Additional support comes from knowledge of 'methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs' and contextual knowledge of 'program sponsors, participants and respondents.' This satisfies the need to confirm detailed requirements and manage competing needs within program constraints.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is relevant because the subprocess requires gathering and elaborating stakeholder data requirements and understanding the conditions under which statistical development and operations will occur. The work description includes attending stakeholder meetings, discussing data requirements with managers, clients and specialists, and translating subject matter requirements into specifications. It also explicitly references governance concepts for protecting and optimizing data assets, which connects to D012, and conformity to standards and data origin, which connects to D006. Evidence includes: 'Attends Departmental meetings, and interdepartmental and stakeholder meetings (as required), to gather data/information'; 'discusses data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients or service providers to comprehend and elaborate the conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur'; 'liaise with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development'; and 'Provides advice, information and guidance to data users and clients regarding governance concepts used to protect and optimize the utility of Statistics Canada’s data assets.' This supports consultation, requirement clarification, standards awareness and governance-informed confirmation of needs.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because confirming stakeholder needs often requires understanding operational constraints, collection conditions, system requirements and impacts on data collection and processing. The work description shows direct engagement with clients, service providers and subject matter specialists to elaborate operational conditions and resolve differences affecting efficiency and quality, which aligns with D012's emphasis on clearer accountabilities, escalation and prioritization when needs conflict. It is less directly focused on metadata/discoverability, so relevance is medium rather than high. Evidence includes: 'Meets with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others, in order to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur. There is a requirement to understand the issues and resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the division's operations and quality of outputs'; 'Provides assistance and advice to users on methods and practices of collection and coding'; and 'Assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems.' This satisfies the subprocess need to confirm feasible, operationally grounded requirements.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role has a lower but still material connection because subprocess 1.2 involves consulting stakeholders and understanding current and future data requirements. The work description includes discussing data requirements with clients and stakeholders, participating in interviews and focus groups, and supporting assessment of current and future requirements for data. These activities align with consultation and needs confirmation, but the role is oriented toward evaluation studies rather than statistical production requirements, metadata/discoverability, or governance of statistical delivery. Evidence includes: 'Provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data'; 'Speaking skills are required to discuss data requirements with Statistics Canada clients and evaluation colleagues'; 'participate in interviews, focus groups and discussions with Statistics Canada clients on data requirements'; and 'Attends departmental and inter-departmental meetings, when required, to discuss files / issues and evaluation requirements.' This supports stakeholder consultation, but only indirectly addresses the specific transformation drivers for this subprocess.

drivers: D005 Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access
D006 Metadata, Data Standards and Discoverability
D010 Modern Statistical Methods and Methodological Innovation
D011 Operational Efficiency and Cost Discipline
D012 Governance, Prioritization and Execution Discipline

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is directly implicated because subprocess 1.3 requires establishing output objectives that include suitability, quality measures, standards compliance and constraints from confidentiality and policy frameworks. The metadata and standards driver is especially central here. The role’s relevant subprocess aspect is defining output objectives that explicitly include metadata completeness, interoperability, dissemination requirements and quality expectations. The needed capability is to translate client and program requirements into metadata specifications, assess metadata quality, and ensure compliance with standards and policies. This work description satisfies that need through duties to 'prepare, edit, validate and disseminate statistical metadata,' 'provide assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines,' and 'assist with statistical metadata quality evaluations.' It also explicitly supports requirement-setting through communication responsibilities to 'develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata' and to 'negotiate procedural modifications, priorities and target dates.' It is also materially connected to privacy and legal constraints because it requires 'awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information to ensure that actions are in compliance.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is strongly connected because establishing output objectives is fundamentally about deciding what outputs will be produced, in what form, with what quality, and for which users, under resource and policy constraints. The relevant subprocess aspect is agreeing output scope, feasibility, dissemination form, quality and user suitability. The needed capability is to interpret user information needs, assess feasibility of outputs, evaluate quality implications, and align dissemination with legal and operational constraints. This work description satisfies that need through key activities to 'edit, validate, market and disseminate data,' 'interpret client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations,' and 'review and assess data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases.' Evidence of direct support to output-objective setting appears in research and analysis responsibilities: 'Interprets user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required,' 'Analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services,' and 'Compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output.' It is also relevant to privacy and governance constraints because it requires knowledge of 'the Statistics Act' and 'particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected because subprocess 1.3 includes establishing output objectives that reflect methodological feasibility, quality targets, subject-matter suitability and resource-constrained trade-offs. The relevant subprocess aspect is determining what outputs are analytically meaningful and feasible given methods, concepts, definitions and program context. The needed capability is subject-matter analysis, assessment of methodological impacts on outputs, and translation of requirements into specifications and plans. This work description satisfies that need through activities to 'participate in the analysis of statistical program data,' 'suggest possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures,' and 'assist in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.' It also directly supports governance and prioritization through communication responsibilities to 'develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development,' 'negotiate procedural modifications' and 'establish project plans, priorities and target dates.' Methodological innovation is explicitly relevant because the role requires 'knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs' and research responsibilities include analyzing 'changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.' Privacy and legal frameworks are also explicitly referenced through awareness of the 'Statistics and Privacy Acts.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because output objectives in subprocess 1.3 must be realistic in light of operational capacity, collection and processing constraints, efficiency pressures and confidentiality requirements. The relevant subprocess aspect is aligning desired outputs and service levels with operational feasibility, quality control and available resources. The needed capability is understanding how collection, coding and processing methods affect output integrity, timeliness, efficiency and quality. This work description satisfies that need through key activities to 'evaluate collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommend alternatives' and to provide reports and recommendations on 'options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems.' It also supports governance and execution discipline through responsibilities to meet with specialists and clients 'to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur' and to resolve issues affecting 'the efficiency of the division's operations and quality of outputs.' Research evidence includes 'Analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results' and 'Assesses and reviews system requirements.' It is also relevant to privacy and legal constraints because it requires awareness of the 'Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because subprocess 1.3 increasingly depends on data quality, standards conformity, governance and modern analytical methods when setting output objectives. The relevant subprocess aspect is assessing whether proposed outputs are supportable through available data, methods, standards and governance controls. The needed capability is data preparation, quality assessment, standards conformity, risk assessment and communication of data requirements into operational specifications. This work description satisfies that need through activities to conduct 'data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin.' It also supports methodological and governance drivers through knowledge of 'data science and its life cycle,' 'survey methodologies, data risk assessment, impact and quantitative analysis,' and 'data stewardship and the ability to assess the quality of data, protect and secure data, and safeguard their responsible use.' Communication evidence includes discussing 'data requirements with operations managers' and liaising 'with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development.' It is somewhat less direct than output- or metadata-focused roles because the position supports studies and projects rather than directly defining output objectives.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role has a weaker but still material connection because subprocess 1.3 involves confirming that output objectives meet user needs and are feasible within resource and policy constraints, and this role contributes to assessing requirements, evidence and cost-benefit considerations. The relevant subprocess aspect is supporting evidence-based determination of requirements and trade-offs. The needed capability is gathering and analyzing information on current and future data requirements, conducting socio-economic and cost-benefit analysis, and communicating findings to management. This work description satisfies that need through duties to 'provide support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data,' 'gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases,' and 'participates in the conduct of socio-economic analyses and cost-benefit analysis of programs.' It also contributes to user-needs understanding through participation in 'interviews, and focus groups' and meetings 'to discuss files / issues and evaluation requirements.' However, the role is primarily oriented to evaluation studies under supervision rather than directly establishing statistical output objectives, metadata standards or dissemination commitments.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This subprocess explicitly requires assessing whether candidate data sources are suitable and available under workable metadata, interoperability, delivery and governance conditions. That maps directly to this role’s responsibility for statistical metadata production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation. The needed capability is to assess metadata availability, standards alignment, machine-readable structures, documentation quality and impacts of modified methods and systems on metadata use. This work description satisfies that need through duties to 'prepare, edit, validate and disseminate statistical metadata,' provide advice on 'documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines,' and 'participate[] in the testing of new procedures and systems.' It also includes interpreting client requirements 'to determine options for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata,' analyzing methods and systems to 'propose enhancements or alternatives,' and evaluating metadata quality across programs. The role is also materially connected to drivers on metadata standards, integrated pipelines, cloud/digital platforms and privacy/security through knowledge of metadata frameworks, repository use, policies, the Statistics Act, and awareness of the Privacy Act and confidentiality requirements.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: GSBPM 1.5 requires checking whether existing and alternative sources can be acquired, ingested, transformed and used for statistical purposes, including quality, standards conformity, origin, governance and operational fit. This role is strongly implicated because it performs core source-readiness and suitability tasks. The needed capability is to assess candidate data sources for acquisition feasibility, quality, conformity to standards, provenance, governance, and suitability for downstream analytical and automated use. This work description satisfies that need through key activities in 'data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin.' It also includes discussing 'data requirements with operations managers... subject matter and systems specialists, clients or service providers to comprehend and elaborate the conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur,' which aligns with assessing source availability conditions and delivery arrangements. Evidence also includes knowledge of 'data capture and acquisition,' 'warehousing,' 'processing,' and 'evolving information sources, survey methodologies, data risk assessment,' plus knowledge of governance, secure and responsible data use, and partnerships used 'to assess data provided by other levels of government for validity and integrity.' This directly supports drivers related to administrative/alternative data, AI and automation, integrated pipelines, standards, privacy/security and efficiency.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This subprocess includes checking source availability conditions, supplier arrangements, formats, delivery, ICT resources, processing implications and legal/privacy constraints. That is closely aligned with this role’s operational assessment of collection, coding and processing methods and systems. The needed capability is to evaluate whether a source can be operationalized within collection and processing workflows, including supplier collaboration, format requirements, system requirements, data flows, and impacts on output integrity. This work description satisfies that need by 'evaluat[ing] collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommend[ing] alternatives,' meeting with 'subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others' to understand operational conditions, and contacting 'data suppliers or respondents' to explain procedures for obtaining data 'in the appropriate format.' It also includes preparing 'reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems,' analyzing 'changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results,' and assessing 'system requirements' for new processing systems. The role further covers knowledge of data flows, systems analysis, databases, external data contacts, and the Statistics Act and Privacy Act. This makes it highly relevant to drivers on integrated pipelines, administrative and alternative data, cloud/platform feasibility, secure access, standards and operational efficiency.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: A central part of GSBPM 1.5 is determining whether available sources are statistically suitable given concepts, definitions, collection conditions, processing constraints and methodological implications. This role is materially connected because it assesses feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs and evaluates how data conditions affect results. The needed capability is methodological and subject-matter assessment of source suitability: whether concepts match requirements, whether collection and storage conditions constrain use, and whether alternative methods or systems are preferable. This work description satisfies that need through knowledge of 'methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling,' and 'methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs.' Strong evidence appears in research responsibilities to 'assess[] and determine[] the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored' and to analyze current methods 'to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.' It also includes liaising to translate subject-matter requirements into system specifications and knowledge of legal/privacy requirements. This aligns strongly with drivers on administrative and alternative data, modern statistical methods, integrated pipelines and efficiency.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: Although this role is more downstream than needs specification, it is still materially connected because GSBPM 1.5 requires assessing whether new or modified systems and databases produce usable, reliable data and whether requested outputs are feasible from available sources. The needed capability is to review data quality and feasibility implications of new databases and processing specifications, and to judge whether available data can support intended outputs. This work description satisfies that need through the key activity 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases' and through research tasks to 'analyze[] and evaluate[] data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness,' 'interpret[] user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required,' and examine 'new or revised processing specifications' for effects on integration and coordination of capture and processing functions. It also includes adapting data to new definitions or formats and knowledge of feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs. Relevance is medium rather than high because the role focuses more on production/dissemination after source selection, but it still contributes important evidence on source suitability, system fit and output feasibility.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This subprocess involves researching existing and alternative data sources, assessing whether they meet requirements, and considering cost-benefit and gap-filling strategies. This role is implicated because it supports assessment of data requirements and source usefulness, though in an evaluation context rather than core statistical production design. The needed capability is to research and compare available data sources, gather and analyze quantitative and qualitative evidence, and support judgments about future data requirements and retrieval improvements. This work description satisfies that need through duties to 'provide[] support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data; gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases,' and to recommend 'enhancements to methods for retrieving data.' Strong evidence also includes research responsibilities where the position 'identifies and recommends... the usefulness and accessible sources of data to be used in studies' and collects data from 'a variety of sources,' including other departments and governments. Communication requirements to discuss 'data requirements' and communicate with stakeholders 'in the data acquisition process' also align with source availability assessment. Relevance is medium because the role addresses source assessment and acquisition, but primarily for evaluation studies rather than enterprise statistical source strategy, metadata, legal frameworks or pipeline integration.
