implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This subprocess is fundamentally about documenting options, costs, benefits, risks, stakeholder impacts and recommendations for approval, which closely aligns with evaluation and business-case style work. The relevant aspect of the subprocess is the need to assemble evidence on the current state, assess future requirements, analyze options, and support senior management decision-making. The capability needed is evaluation research, socio-economic and cost-benefit analysis, synthesis of qualitative and quantitative evidence, and preparation of briefing/report material for management and governance review. This work description satisfies that need because it explicitly includes participation in evaluation studies of programs, policies and initiatives; support for assessing current and future data requirements; conducting socio-economic analyses and cost-benefit analysis; determining implications of findings; and providing supporting data for reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda for senior management. Evidence includes: 'Provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data'; 'participates in the conduct of socio-economic analyses and cost-benefit analysis of programs'; 'applying analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of evaluation results and formulating conclusions'; and 'Provides the Evaluation Manager with supporting data for sections of reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda for senior management'. These responsibilities are materially connected to preparing and submitting a business case under strong governance, efficiency and transformation drivers.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: A business case for a new or modified statistical process must address metadata investment, standards, interoperability, discoverability, documentation, quality and policy compliance, especially under the metadata and standards driver and reusable architecture drivers. The relevant aspect of the subprocess is documenting the proposed 'To-Be' solution and its enterprise implications, including metadata repository use, standards adoption, procedural changes, quality impacts and client requirements. The capability needed is understanding metadata frameworks, assessing impacts of modified methods and systems, translating requirements into specifications, and advising on metadata-related policies and quality. This work description satisfies that need because it covers preparing and validating metadata, advising clients on standards and policies, analyzing current and proposed methods and systems, interpreting requirements into options, and contributing to reports and documentation. Evidence includes: 'develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata'; 'Knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks... and how those concepts and frameworks are used and reflected in policies, methods and procedures'; 'Interprets client requirements in order to determine options'; and 'Analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives.' This is materially relevant where the business case must justify metadata capability, standards alignment and enterprise reuse, though it is narrower than the core evaluation/business-case role.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: The subprocess requires evidence on data readiness, analytical feasibility, automation opportunities, data quality, governance and risks for proposed process changes. The relevant aspect is assessing the current and future analytical and data environment that underpins the business case, especially for AI, automation, alternative data, open-source tools and operational efficiency. The capability needed is data analysis across the data lifecycle, assessment of data quality and risk, translation of requirements into specifications, and preparation of analytical briefings for decision-makers. This work description satisfies that need because it supports studies and projects using statistical analysis tools, performs data extraction/cleansing/transformation/validation, advises on governance concepts, discusses data requirements with managers and specialists, and has knowledge of data science lifecycle, data risk assessment, cost-benefit analysis and secure/responsible data use. Evidence includes: 'Supports the conduct of studies and/or projects'; 'Conducts data preparation techniques... data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation'; 'discusses data requirements with operations managers... subject matter and systems specialists'; 'knowledge of data science and its life cycle'; and 'knowledge of... data risk assessment... and cost benefit analysis'. This supports the evidence base for a business case, though the role is less directly accountable for formal option appraisal and approval documentation.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: Preparing a business case requires a clear description of the current 'As-Is' process, operational inefficiencies, system requirements, options for manual versus automated operations, and implications for collection and processing. The relevant aspect of the subprocess is documenting operational realities, identifying issues to be addressed, and specifying requirements and alternatives for future-state operations under automation, orchestration, privacy and efficiency drivers. The capability needed is operational process knowledge, evaluation of methods and procedures, requirements analysis, and reporting on options and operational constraints. This work description satisfies that need because it participates in manual and automated operations, evaluates methods and procedures, recommends alternatives, prepares reports outlining options and requirements, and assesses system requirements for new processing systems. Evidence includes: 'Participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations'; 'Evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives'; 'Prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems'; and 'Assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers'. It is materially connected because business cases depend on credible operational baselines and future operational design considerations.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This subprocess requires feasibility and impact assessment of new or modified statistical programs, analysis of methodological and technological changes, and development of recommendations for decision-makers. The relevant aspect is the preparation of option analysis and recommendations for approval, including impacts of changed methods, systems, definitions, constraints and stakeholder context. The capability needed is subject-matter and methodological analysis, feasibility assessment, impact assessment, translation of requirements into development specifications, and understanding of program context and sponsors. This work description satisfies that need because it explicitly includes knowledge and analysis related to the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs, liaison to translate requirements into specifications and establish project plans, and analysis of changes in procedures, methodology and technology to determine effects on outputs and services. Evidence includes: 'Knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs'; 'Liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development... and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates'; and 'Analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.' This is strongly implicated because business cases must compare options and justify recommended changes in statistical production.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: A business case for process change must consider downstream effects on data products, dissemination, client service, system integration, feasibility of user requirements, and impacts of revised processing specifications. The relevant aspect of the subprocess is assessing how proposed changes affect outputs, services, dissemination arrangements and user needs in the 'To-Be' design. The capability needed is analysis of feasibility and impact of modified statistical programs, interpretation of user requirements into options, and assessment of effects of procedural and technological changes on outputs and services. This work description satisfies that need because it reviews data quality from new and modified systems, provides consultative services to users, interprets requests to determine feasibility and options, and analyzes changes in procedures, methodology and technology for their effect on outputs, products and services. Evidence includes: 'Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases'; 'Knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to prepare information for studies and to review the feasibility and potential impact of new or modified statistical programs'; 'Interprets user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options'; and 'Analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.' This is materially relevant to business-case preparation, though more focused on downstream production/dissemination implications than on the full approval case.

drivers: Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access
Modular Reusable Architecture and Self-Service Tools

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is directly implicated because subprocess 2.1 is about designing statistical outputs and dissemination, with strong emphasis on metadata, standards, discoverability, dissemination procedures, and secure/confidential access. The role’s relevant aspect is the design and operationalization of metadata for production, storage and dissemination of outputs. The subprocess needs capability to translate dissemination and metadata requirements into specifications, apply standards, evaluate metadata quality, and adapt metadata to new systems and formats. This role satisfies that need through duties to 'prepare, edit, validate and disseminate statistical metadata,' ensure metadata is 'correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository,' and provide 'assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines.' It also explicitly supports design change by 'provid[ing] feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata' and 'participat[ing] in the testing of new procedures and systems.' Evidence also aligns strongly with drivers D006 and D004: the role has 'knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks used within Statistics Canada, the Government of Canada and internationally,' knowledge of 'methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata,' and liaises to 'develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.' It is also materially connected to D005 because it requires awareness of 'the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is highly relevant because subprocess 2.1 explicitly concerns the detailed design of statistical outputs, products, services, dissemination tools and procedures, including access to confidential outputs. The relevant aspect is the shaping of dissemination products, custom outputs, user-facing data services, and adaptation of outputs to changing methods, systems and source data. The subprocess needs capability to interpret user requirements, design feasible output products, assess impacts of system and methodology changes on outputs, and ensure dissemination complies with policy and confidentiality requirements. This work description satisfies that need through core activities to 'edit, validate, market and disseminate data,' 'interpret client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations,' 'review and assess data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases,' and 'provide statistical data and consultative services to users.' Evidence of direct design relevance includes research responsibilities to 'compile data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output,' 'analyze changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services,' and 'adapt data to new definitions or presentation formats.' It also supports drivers D003, D004, D007, D009 and D011 through adapting outputs to new sources and formats, and D005 through required awareness of 'the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is materially connected because subprocess 2.1 includes designing outputs and dissemination products in ways that reflect subject-matter meaning, methodological constraints, and changes in technology, procedures and source conditions. The relevant aspect is analytical and subject-matter input into how outputs should be presented, defined and adjusted. The subprocess needs capability to assess how concepts, definitions, collection conditions and methodological changes affect outputs, products and services. This role satisfies that need by participating in analysis for 'publication purposes,' suggesting feedback on 'collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures,' and providing assistance to users. The strongest evidence is in research and analysis: the role 'analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services,' 'assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored,' and 'analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.' It also includes liaison to 'develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development,' which supports dissemination design under changing digital and data-source drivers.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because subprocess 2.1 includes designing the systems, tools and procedures used later in dissemination, and because dissemination design depends on operational feasibility, output quality, and confidentiality controls. The relevant aspect is operational design input on methods, procedures, systems requirements and output preparation. The subprocess needs capability to evaluate operational methods, understand system/data-flow implications, and prepare standardized output products and supporting procedures. This work description satisfies that need through activities to 'evaluate collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommend alternatives,' provide advice on methods and practices, and contribute to training materials. Evidence directly tied to output/dissemination design includes 'designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications,' 'prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems,' and 'meets with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others, in order to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur.' It also has contextual knowledge of 'systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows' and analyzes 'changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results.' Security relevance is present through awareness of the 'Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is relevant because several drivers for subprocess 2.1 concern AI and automation, administrative and alternative data, digital platforms, dashboards, and standards-based outputs. The relevant aspect is preparing, validating and structuring data so that dissemination products can be designed around reliable, standards-conformant and secure data assets. The subprocess needs capability in data preparation, quality assessment, standards conformance, visualization-oriented reporting, and governance for secure and responsible use of data. This work description satisfies that need through activities to conduct 'data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin' and through knowledge of the data science lifecycle including 'summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence.' It also explicitly supports modern dissemination design by requiring writing skills to develop 'analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools' and communication with specialists and users to 'develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development.' Driver alignment is especially strong for D001, D003, D004 and D009, and there is also security/governance relevance because the role includes 'data stewardship,' ability to 'protect and secure data,' and 'basic knowledge of ... policies pertaining to the handling, tracking, filing and storing of sensitive and confidential material.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role has a limited but still material connection to subprocess 2.1 because output and dissemination design can be informed by evidence on user needs, data requirements, performance and reporting. The relevant aspect is evaluative support for understanding information requirements and contributing to reports and presentations, rather than direct design of dissemination products or metadata systems. The subprocess needs some capability to assess requirements, synthesize evidence, and support reporting on implications of methods and data choices. This work description partially satisfies that need through activities to 'provide support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data,' 'identify, gather, analyze and synthesize quantitative and qualitative data,' and 'provide the Evaluation Manager with supporting data for sections of reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda.' However, the role is not primarily responsible for dissemination design, metadata standards, secure access design, or output-system specification. Its relevance is therefore low, based mainly on its research, reporting and stakeholder-discussion functions rather than direct output/dissemination responsibilities.

drivers: D006 Metadata, Data Standards and Discoverability
D010 Modern Statistical Methods and Methodological Innovation

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is directly implicated because subprocess 2.2 requires preparation of metadata for collected and derived variables, classifications, code lists and standards alignment. The subprocess specifically emphasizes that metadata preparation is a necessary precondition for later phases and that national and international standards should be followed. This position provides the capability to prepare, edit, validate and disseminate statistical metadata and to ensure it is loaded to the corporate metadata repository. It also supports standards-based variable design by advising clients on 'statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines.' The role is materially connected to driver D006 because it requires 'knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks used within Statistics Canada, the Government of Canada and internationally' and knowledge of policies and procedures for metadata production, storage, dissemination and evaluation. It is also relevant to D003 because aligning administrative and alternative data to statistical concepts depends on interpreting client requirements and adapting metadata to changed methods and systems; evidence includes 'interprets client requirements in order to determine options for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata' and 'analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems... to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is strongly connected because variable design in 2.2 is interdependent with collection design and must account for concepts, definitions, classifications and operational implementation. The subprocess includes defining variables to be collected, unit types, and classifications, and notes parallel work with collection design. This position evaluates collection and coding methods, recommends alternatives, and works on collection and processing operations, which is relevant where variable definitions must be operationalized in instruments and coding structures. The needed capability is understanding how concepts and classifications function in collection and coding environments, especially when administrative or alternative data introduce inconsistent definitions and unit structures under driver D003. Evidence includes 'Participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' 'Evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives,' and analysis of 'problems encountered in implementing concepts, definitions, classifications and other instructions.' It also supports D010 because the role 'assesses and reviews system requirements' and analyzes changes to data sources and outputs to determine impacts on integrity and completeness.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially implicated because subprocess 2.2 requires subject-matter definition of variables, derived variables, concepts, classifications and unit structures, including assessing how definitions and collection conditions affect outputs. The role provides capability in subject-matter concepts, statistical methods, and assessing impacts of concepts and definitions on results. This is especially relevant to D003 and D010, where administrative and alternative data require mapping non-statistical concepts to statistical concepts, and methodological innovation may require redesign of collected and derived variables. Evidence includes communication responsibility to 'develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development,' knowledge of 'methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling,' and research responsibilities that 'assess and determine the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored.' It also explicitly analyzes 'current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems,' which aligns with redesigning variables and classifications.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because subprocess 2.2 increasingly depends on data-oriented design choices shaped by administrative and alternative data, standards conformance, and innovative methods. The needed capability is understanding data structures, transformation, validation, standards conformity, and how subject-matter requirements become data specifications. This position supports those needs through data preparation, quality assessment, and translating requirements into specifications. Evidence includes 'Conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin' and communication responsibilities to 'discuss data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists' and 'develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development.' It is particularly relevant to D003 because administrative and alternative data often require transformation and validation against statistical concepts, and to D010 because the role requires knowledge of the data science lifecycle, modeling, and survey methodologies. Relevance is medium rather than high because the description is more focused on analysis and data handling than on formal variable and metadata design ownership.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is connected because variable design affects downstream editing, validation, adaptation to new definitions, and integration of processing specifications. The subprocess requires well-defined variables, classifications and metadata so that later production and dissemination can function consistently. The needed capability is assessing how new definitions, revised specifications and multiple data sources affect data validity and output structures. Evidence includes 'Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases,' 'Examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions,' and 'Adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats, depending on the complexity of the subject matter or the number of different sources.' This is relevant to D003 because administrative and alternative data often require adaptation across sources and definitions, and to D010 because methodological or system changes affect output design. Relevance is medium because the role is more downstream from variable design, but still materially connected through specification impacts and definition changes.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role has a limited but still material connection to subprocess 2.2 through assessing data requirements and analyzing quantitative and qualitative data for studies. The subprocess requires identifying what variables are needed and documenting them, and this role contributes to understanding current and future data requirements. Evidence includes 'Provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data; gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases' and communication on 'discuss data requirements with Statistics Canada clients and evaluation colleagues.' However, the work description does not show direct responsibility for defining statistical variables, classifications, unit types, or metadata standards. Its connection is therefore indirect and mainly supportive rather than central.

drivers: Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration
Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access
Modular Reusable Architecture and Self-Service Tools
Modern Statistical Methods and Methodological Innovation

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is directly connected to collection design because the subprocess concerns preparing collection strategies, instruments, methods, fieldwork operations, respondent engagement, and monitoring arrangements. The work description explicitly covers participation in 'the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data' and 'evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives,' which aligns closely with designing collection methods and operational approaches. The subprocess also requires capability to advise on collection practices, operationalize collection procedures, and support workforce adoption of new methods; this role provides 'assistance and advice to users on methods and practices of collection and coding' and 'provides input to training materials concerning data collection operations and assists in training delivery.' Drivers such as AI and Automation, Integrated Data Pipelines, Administrative and Alternative Data, and Operational Efficiency are reflected in the role's responsibility for manual and automated operations, assessing system requirements, and analyzing changes to data sources and outputs. Evidence includes 'prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems,' 'meets with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others, in order to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur,' and 'contacts data suppliers or respondents... explain technical procedures for obtaining the data in the appropriate format.' Security and privacy aspects of collection design are also supported by the requirement for awareness of 'the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: Design collection is materially shaped by metadata capture at source, standardized structures, interoperable exchange, documentation, and traceable agreements. This role is highly implicated because it focuses on producing, validating, evaluating, and advising on statistical metadata, which is central to drivers such as Metadata, Data Standards and Discoverability, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Administrative and Alternative Data. The subprocess requires collection instruments, APIs, transfer specifications, and monitoring mechanisms to support standardized metadata and downstream reuse; this role 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata,' 'provides assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines,' and 'provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata.' The needed capability is to translate collection and program requirements into metadata specifications and assess impacts of procedural or system changes. The work description explicitly states the role 'liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.' It also supports change monitoring and quality evaluation through evidence such as 'analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems... to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats' and 'evaluates selected indicators of statistical metadata quality across survey and statistical programs.' Privacy and compliance needs in collection design are also addressed through awareness of 'the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This subprocess increasingly involves API-based acquisition, automated transfers, alternative data intake, data validation, and quality controls at the point of collection design. This role is implicated because it brings capability in data capture, acquisition, extraction, validation, standards conformance, and risk assessment that informs how collection methods should be designed under drivers such as AI and Automation, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Administrative and Alternative Data, and Operational Efficiency. The work description states that the role 'conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin,' which is relevant to designing collection arrangements that produce usable, standards-conformant inputs. The subprocess also needs communication with operations and systems stakeholders to define collection conditions and specifications; this role 'discusses data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients or service providers to comprehend and elaborate the conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur' and 'liaise[s] with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development.' The role further supports secure and governed collection design through knowledge of 'data stewardship,' ability to 'protect and secure data,' and knowledge of policies for 'handling, tracking, filing and storing of sensitive and confidential material.' It is medium rather than high because the description is broader data analytics support rather than explicit ownership of collection instrument or collection operations design.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: Design collection requires methodological judgment about how data should be gathered, how respondent and subject-matter context affects collection, and how changes in methods or technology alter collection quality and feasibility. This role is implicated because it explicitly contributes feedback on collection methods and analyzes the effects of methodological and procedural changes. The work description states that the incumbent 'participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.' That directly supports the subprocess need to design appropriate collection instruments and strategies, including adaptive or multi-mode approaches under the Modern Statistical Methods and Methodological Innovation driver. The subprocess also requires translation of subject-matter requirements into operational specifications; this role 'liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development.' Relevant capability includes understanding survey universe, respondents, and collection conditions, which is evidenced by 'knowledge of the subject and universe of the survey is required in order to propose suitable changes to statistical or reporting methods and techniques' and 'knowledge of program context, program sponsors, participants and respondents.' It also supports assessment of impacts from new technologies and procedures through 'analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output' and 'analyzes current collection... methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role has a limited but material connection to collection design through assessing data requirements, identifying sources, participating in interviews and focus groups, and recommending enhancements to data retrieval methods. The subprocess emphasizes understanding respondents, incorporating user perspectives, and selecting appropriate sources and methods. The work description supports those needs by stating the role 'provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data; gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases' and 'recommends... enhancements to methods for retrieving data.' It also includes participation in 'interviews, and focus groups,' which is relevant to respondent or stakeholder input into collection design. Communication requirements such as discussing 'data requirements with Statistics Canada clients and evaluation colleagues' and communicating 'with clients in the data acquisition process' provide some alignment with designing collection approaches and agreements. However, the role is primarily focused on evaluation studies rather than statistical collection design itself, so the connection is low.

drivers: Modern Statistical Methods and Methodological Innovation

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected because subprocess 2.4 depends on well-defined frames, registers, classifications, identifiers and metadata to specify the population of interest, integrate administrative/register sources, and document frame construction and coverage assessment. The capability needed is statistical metadata management, standards application, and translation of program requirements into metadata specifications. This work description satisfies that need through responsibilities to "prepare, edit, validate and disseminate statistical metadata," provide advice on "documented standards and relevant policies," and participate in methods and systems for metadata production and evaluation. It directly references knowledge of "statistical metadata concepts and frameworks," "survey and statistical program subject matter concepts and methodologies," and analysis to "determine options for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata" and to assess impacts of modified methods and procedures. These elements strongly align with driver D006 and also support D003 by enabling integration and reuse of register-based and administrative frames.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because subprocess 2.4 requires analysis of source data, frame construction inputs, coverage assessment, auxiliary data use, and potentially predictive or optimization methods for sample design. The needed capability is quantitative analysis, data preparation, quality assessment, and use of modern analytical tools across varied data sources. This work description satisfies that need by supporting studies using "quantitative statistical data analysis methods and software such as Python, SAS, STATA, R," conducting "data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin," and discussing data requirements with operations managers and specialists. Evidence also includes knowledge of the "data science life cycle," including "predictive analysis," "modeling," and "clustering," plus knowledge of "survey methodologies, data risk assessment, impact and quantitative analysis" and "statistical sampling." These responsibilities align strongly with drivers D001, D003, D010 and D011, especially where administrative/alternative data and AI-supported methods influence frame construction and efficient sample design.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected because subprocess 2.4 requires methodological assessment of the survey universe, data sources, estimation implications, and the effects of concepts and definitions on representativeness and frame quality. The needed capability is subject-matter and methodological analysis to assess feasibility and impacts of modified statistical programs and methods. This work description satisfies that need through participation in analysis of statistical program data, suggesting feedback on "collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures," and assisting in recommendations for improvements to "survey methods and activities." Evidence includes knowledge of "methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation," "methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs," and "knowledge of the subject and universe of the survey" to "propose suitable changes to statistical or reporting methods and techniques." Its research component also includes analyzing "changes in procedures, methodology" and assessing impacts of "different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored." This strongly supports D010 and D003, and also D011 where redesign affects efficiency and quality.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is connected because subprocess 2.4 informs downstream collection operations and requires practical understanding of data sources, collection methods, and operational implications of frame and sample choices. The needed capability is operational assessment of collection methods, data sources, and system requirements to ensure the designed frame/sample can be implemented efficiently and with quality. This work description satisfies that need by "evaluat[ing] collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommend[ing] alternatives," providing advice on collection methods, and preparing reports on requirements for "statistical collection and processing systems." Evidence includes knowledge of "the concepts, methods and techniques used in the management and control of statistical collection," knowledge of "data sources," and research responsibilities that "analyse changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results" and report on "how the survey was conducted" including problems with concepts, definitions and classifications. This is relevant particularly to D011 and D003, though the role is more operationally downstream than directly responsible for sample design.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated to the extent that subprocess 2.4 relies on assessing source data quality, integrating diverse sources, and understanding effects of methodological or system changes on statistical outputs. The needed capability is evaluation of data validity, feasibility of modified programs, and adaptation of data from multiple sources and definitions. This work description satisfies that need through responsibilities to "review and assess data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases" and research activities that "compile data from diverse sources," "analyze and evaluate data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness," and "adapt data to new definitions or presentation formats" depending on source complexity. It also includes knowledge of "methods, techniques, practices and procedures to prepare information for studies and to review the feasibility and potential impact of new or modified statistical programs." This supports subprocess needs around frame-source assessment and integration under drivers D003, D006 and D010, although the role is more focused on downstream data production than direct frame/sample methodology.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role has a limited but still material connection because subprocess 2.4 may require assessment of data requirements, source usefulness, and methodological implications, especially when evaluating alternative frame sources or cost-benefit trade-offs. The needed capability is research into data sources and analytical support for assessing requirements and methods. This work description satisfies that need only indirectly through tasks to "conduct literature and data research," "identify, gather, analyze and synthesize quantitative and qualitative data," "provide support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data," and recommend "enhancements to methods for retrieving data." Evidence also includes identifying "the usefulness and accessible sources of data to be used in studies." However, the role is centered on program evaluation rather than statistical frame construction or sample design, so relevance is low.

drivers: Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration
Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access
Modular Reusable Architecture and Self-Service Tools
Modern Statistical Methods and Methodological Innovation

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This subprocess is directly concerned with designing routines and rules for processing and analysis, including coding, editing, imputation, validation, integration, estimation and analytical methods. This role is strongly implicated because it performs core processing-oriented activities that align with those design concerns: it 'conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin.' The subprocess also has strong drivers around AI and automation, integrated pipelines, administrative and alternative data, open-source tools, and modern methods. The role explicitly requires 'knowledge of data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence, and exploratory/ confirmatory, predictive analysis, regression, text mining, and qualitative analysis.' That capability is materially relevant to designing automated and model-based processing and analysis methods. The role also supports translation of requirements into specifications, as it 'liaise[s] with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development,' which is central to designing reproducible processing rules and analytical workflows. Its knowledge of 'survey methodologies, data risk assessment' and ability to 'assess the quality of data and identify and mitigate risks to its integrity' also supports validation and source-specific processing design. Privacy and secure handling are relevant as well, given the requirement for 'data stewardship' and to 'protect and secure data.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected because the subprocess explicitly includes design of processing routines for coding, editing, validation and integration, and this position works in the operational domain of 'manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data.' It also 'evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives,' which directly matches the need to design or redesign processing methods under drivers such as automation, integrated pipelines and efficiency. The role brings capability in 'methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications,' which is directly relevant to designing validation checkpoints and quality controls. It also requires 'knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows, general software packages and computer languages, for designing the specifications for testing of applications, the application and conversion of databases, and the maintenance and use of databases both for regular production of statistical data and for ad hoc manipulations and retrievals.' That is strong evidence of relevance to integrated data pipelines, orchestration, and source integration design. The role further 'assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems,' showing responsibility for translating operational and methodological needs into processing specifications. Privacy and confidentiality drivers are also implicated because the role requires awareness of 'the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This subprocess is about designing the statistical methodology used in later Process and Analyse phases, including estimation, editing, validation and analysis. This role is highly relevant because it explicitly participates in methodological feedback and improvement: it 'participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.' That is a direct connection to processing and analysis design. The role also requires 'knowledge of statistical or economic theory and principles and the relevance of their application in a computerized environment, and the methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling,' which aligns with the subprocess emphasis on estimation and analytical method design, especially under drivers for AI, modern statistical methods and automation. It further includes 'knowledge of the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data,' which is relevant to validation design and assessing impacts of alternative processing approaches. The research component is also directly aligned: it 'analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems' and 'analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.' This supports design choices influenced by integrated pipelines, new data sources, and methodological innovation. Security and confidentiality are also relevant through explicit awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is strongly implicated because the subprocess is heavily affected by metadata-driven processing, standards-based integration, lineage, harmonization and validation rules. The role directly supports those needs by preparing and validating metadata and by helping translate requirements into metadata specifications: it 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository' and 'liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.' This is directly relevant to the driver on metadata, data standards and discoverability. The subprocess also includes design of integration from multiple sources and validation rules; this role requires 'knowledge of survey and statistical program subject matter concepts and methodologies relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data in order to assess client requirements for metadata production, storage and dissemination.' It also 'analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives' and 'interprets client requirements in order to determine options for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata and in order to determine the possible impacts of proposed modifications in methods and procedures.' Those responsibilities support the design of standardized, reusable and orchestrated processing environments. The role is also relevant to privacy and secure access because it requires awareness of 'the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because the subprocess includes design of validation, processing specifications, integration logic and adaptation of outputs to new sources and formats. The role performs downstream production functions that depend on such designs and also contributes to assessing and shaping them. Evidence includes that it 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data' and 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases.' It also 'examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems,' which is materially relevant to integrated pipelines and orchestration. The role further 'adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats, depending on the complexity of the subject matter or the number of different sources,' which connects to administrative and alternative data and harmonization across sources. Its knowledge of 'methods, techniques, practices and procedures to prepare information for studies and to review the feasibility and potential impact of new or modified statistical programs' and of assessing 'the validity of collected and processed data' supports the subprocess need for validation and processing design feedback. Relevance is medium rather than high because the role is more focused on production, validation and dissemination than on primary methodological design.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role has some connection to the subprocess through analysis of quantitative and qualitative data and recommendations on methods for retrieving data, but it is not primarily focused on designing statistical processing and analysis methods for production. Relevant evidence includes that it 'identif[ies], gather[s], analyz[es] and synthesiz[es] quantitative and qualitative data' and 'recommends to the Evaluation Manager, enhancements to methods for retrieving data as well as information used in the conduct of socio-economic analyses and cost-benefit analyses.' It also has knowledge of 'theories and principles of economics, socio-economic, demography and statistics' and research methods. However, the role is centered on program evaluation studies rather than on designing coding, editing, imputation, integration, validation, estimation or disclosure control methods for statistical production. Therefore it is only indirectly implicated.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is directly implicated because subprocess 2.6 is about designing end-to-end production workflows, systems, repositories, responsibilities and reuse, and the drivers strongly emphasize metadata services, standards, discoverability, integration and secure enterprise architecture. The relevant subprocess aspect is the design of production systems that fit together efficiently and reuse shared services. The needed capability is to translate metadata requirements into production/storage/dissemination specifications, assess impacts of changed methods and systems, and support enterprise metadata repositories and quality controls. This work description satisfies that need through explicit responsibilities to "prepare, edit, validate and disseminate statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository," to "provide feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata," and to "participate[] in the testing of new procedures and systems." It also includes communication responsibilities to "develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata" and to "negotiate procedural modifications, priorities and target dates," which aligns closely with workflow architecture, orchestration and governance. It further evidences capability in standards and secure design through knowledge of "statistical metadata concepts and frameworks," "methods, procedures and systems," consistency "across programs," and awareness of the "Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information."

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected because subprocess 2.6 explicitly covers workflow design from collection through processing, system interactions, operational responsibilities, and efficient fit across processes. The drivers on orchestration, automation, external data integration, cloud/platforms, security, efficiency and governance all point to operational workflow and system design. The relevant subprocess aspect is the design and maintenance of manual and automated operational workflows for collection, coding and processing, including interfaces, testing requirements, data flows and training. The needed capability is operational systems analysis, evaluation of methods and procedures, specification of requirements for new or revised processing systems, and understanding of staff/system interactions. This work description satisfies that need by stating the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," and "prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems." It also directly references workflow/system design evidence through knowledge of "systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows" and research responsibilities that "assess[] and review[] system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems." Security and governance needs are also covered through knowledge of the Statistics Act, Privacy Act, and confidentiality requirements.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because subprocess 2.6 includes designing workflows and systems that support statistical production methods, handoffs, specifications and improvements across collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation. The drivers on methodological innovation, orchestration, governance and efficiency make roles that translate subject-matter requirements into system and process specifications highly relevant. The relevant subprocess aspect is the redesign or adjustment of production methods and workflows to support new or improved statistical programs. The needed capability is to analyze impacts of procedural and technological changes, propose alternative systems, and convert subject-matter requirements into development specifications and plans. This work description satisfies that need through explicit communication responsibilities to "develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," "suggest improvements to ongoing programs," and "establish project plans, priorities and target dates." It also contains strong workflow-design evidence in research and analysis: "Analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services" and "Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems." Its contextual knowledge of program context, data sources, and privacy/security obligations further supports design of governed end-to-end production workflows.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is directly relevant because subprocess 2.6 spans workflow design from upstream processing to downstream dissemination, including integration across divisional systems, revised processing specifications, and user-facing outputs. The drivers on integrated pipelines, digital platforms, metadata/standards, efficiency and governance all affect how production and dissemination components are designed to work together. The relevant subprocess aspect is ensuring that production and dissemination systems are coordinated, that new or modified systems are assessed for quality and integration, and that outputs can be adapted to new formats and requirements. The needed capability is to assess effects of system and procedure changes on output and integration, translate requirements into system specifications, and support dissemination workflows and training. This work description satisfies that need by stating the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," "participates on data production and dissemination teams," and "provides input to training material." It also explicitly supports system/workflow design through liaison to "develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development" and analysis that "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems." Security and governed production are also evidenced by knowledge of the Statistics Act, Privacy Act and policies for dissemination.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because many drivers for subprocess 2.6 require workflows that support data preparation, standards conformance, governance, analytics tooling, and interaction with operations managers and systems specialists. The relevant subprocess aspect is the design of production workflows that include extraction, cleansing, transformation, validation, quality checks and data stewardship within integrated pipelines. The needed capability is practical understanding of the data lifecycle, data preparation stages, governance, risk and translation of requirements into specifications for data development. This work description satisfies that need through key activities in "data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin." It also includes communication responsibilities to "discuss[] data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists" and to "develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development." Its knowledge requirements explicitly cover the "data science life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing" as well as "data stewardship," protecting and securing data, and governance concepts. Relevance is medium rather than high because the role supports and informs workflow design, but the description is less explicitly centered on end-to-end production system architecture than the operational, metadata and production/dissemination roles.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role has a limited but material connection because subprocess 2.6 includes assessing whether existing solutions are fit for purpose and identifying gaps, and some drivers emphasize governance, efficiency, future requirements and evidence-based redesign. The relevant subprocess aspect is the evaluation of current and future data requirements and the identification of improvements to methods for retrieving data. The needed capability is analytical assessment of data sources, requirements and retrieval methods to inform workflow or system redesign decisions. This work description satisfies that need through responsibilities to "provide[] support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data; gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases" and to "recommend[] to the Evaluation Manager, enhancements to methods for retrieving data." It also includes research across diverse sources and communication on data requirements. Relevance is low because the role is primarily focused on program evaluation studies rather than designing statistical production systems and workflows themselves.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is directly connected to building and reusing collection instruments because the subprocess concerns creating, configuring, testing and maintaining instruments used to collect data, and this position explicitly works in collection operations. The relevant subprocess aspects include manual and automated collection instruments, testing and maintenance of collection processes, evaluation of collection methods, and preparation of operational guidance. The capability needed is operational responsibility for collection methods, system requirements, testing specifications, training materials, and secure handling of collected data. This position satisfies that need because it 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' 'evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives,' and 'provides assistance and advice to users on methods and practices of collection and coding.' It also supports instrument build/test and downstream integration through 'knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows' and by 'assess[ing] and review[ing] system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems.' The drivers are strongly reflected: integrated pipelines and reusable architecture through system requirements and data flows; administrative/alternative data through changing data sources; metadata/standards and methodological innovation through reporting on 'problems encountered in implementing concepts, definitions, classifications and other instructions'; and cyber/privacy through explicit awareness of 'the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is materially implicated because the subprocess explicitly emphasizes connecting collection instruments to metadata systems at source, using standard variables/classifications, and capturing metadata and paradata during collection. The relevant subprocess aspects are metadata integration, standards-based instrument design, testing of procedures and systems, and metadata quality evaluation. The capability needed is expertise in statistical metadata frameworks, repository loading, standards, client requirement translation, and testing of metadata-related systems and procedures. This position satisfies that need because it 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository,' 'provides assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines,' and 'participates in the testing of new procedures and systems.' It also directly supports instrument-to-metadata linkage by liaising 'to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.' Evidence of fit with the drivers is especially strong for Metadata, Data Standards and Discoverability, since the role requires 'knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks' and 'methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata.' It also supports integrated pipelines and operational efficiency through analysis of impacts of modified methods and systems, and supports privacy/security through awareness of 'the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is implicated because the subprocess includes collection instruments that are not only questionnaires but also extraction routines, APIs, service interfaces, prefill mechanisms and richer paradata capture, all of which require data extraction, transformation, validation and standards conformance. The relevant subprocess aspects are building extraction-based instruments, validating captured data, supporting automated ingestion, and working with collection operations and system specialists to define requirements. The capability needed is technical data handling across the data lifecycle, including extraction, cleansing, transformation, validation, standards conformance, and communication of requirements into specifications. This position satisfies that need because it 'conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin' and has knowledge of 'data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing' as part of the data science lifecycle. It also interfaces with collection instrument design context by 'discuss[ing] data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists' and by liaising 'to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development.' This aligns particularly with drivers for AI and Automation, Administrative and Alternative Data, Integrated Data Pipelines, and Open-Source/Business Development Enablement. Relevance is medium rather than high because the role is more focused on data preparation and analytics support than direct ownership of collection instrument build.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is implicated because the subprocess includes preparing and testing collection instrument content and functioning, and ensuring that collection methods, concepts and definitions remain suitable as programs evolve. The relevant subprocess aspects are feedback on collection methods, translation of subject-matter requirements into system specifications, and analysis of how collection conditions affect outputs. The capability needed is subject-matter and methodological expertise to assess whether collection instruments capture the right concepts, support valid data gathering, and should be modified in response to changing requirements or technologies. This position satisfies that need because it 'participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.' It also 'liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development' and has 'knowledge of the subject and universe of the survey ... in order to propose suitable changes to statistical or reporting methods and techniques.' Further evidence is its research responsibility to 'analyze current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.' This aligns with drivers for Modern Statistical Methods, Metadata/standards implementation through concepts and definitions, and Operational Efficiency through method improvement. Relevance is medium because the role informs and improves collection instrument design rather than directly building instruments.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description has a secondary connection to the subprocess because collection instruments in 3.1 must integrate with downstream data capture and processing functions, and this role assesses effects of revised processing specifications on those integrations. The relevant subprocess aspects are downstream compatibility of collection instruments, integration of data capture with processing systems, and adaptation to new formats or definitions. The capability needed is understanding of how revised system concepts and processing specifications affect data capture and processing coordination. This position satisfies that need because it 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases' and 'examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems.' It also 'liaises with other specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development.' This supports drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration and Operational Efficiency. Relevance is low because the role is centered on post-collection data production and dissemination rather than direct construction or testing of collection instruments.
