implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is strongly implicated because subprocess 3.2 is about reusing or building components for processing and analysis, and this position directly supports data preparation, transformation, validation and analytical processing using statistical and programming tools. The subprocess requires capability to implement reusable processing logic, analytical routines, and pipeline-ready components influenced by AI, automation, integrated pipelines, alternative data and open-source tooling. This work description satisfies that need through explicit responsibilities for 'data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin' and through use of tools such as 'Python, SAS, STATA, R'. It also requires knowledge of the full data science lifecycle including 'data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization, reporting, visualization' and 'predictive analysis, regression, text mining'. These are materially connected to building processing and analysis components, including AI-enabled and reusable analytical modules. The role also includes governance, protection and secure use of data, supporting drivers on privacy and secure access.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is highly relevant because subprocess 3.2 explicitly includes reuse or build of services such as metadata management services, and several drivers emphasize metadata, standards, discoverability, interoperability and reusable processing. The subprocess needs capability to ensure components consume and produce standardized metadata, preserve lineage, and support metadata-driven processing across programs. This work description directly satisfies that need by 'prepar[ing], edit[ing], validat[ing] and disseminat[ing] statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository' and by providing advice on 'documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines'. It also participates in 'testing of new procedures and systems' and provides feedback on methods for 'producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata'. Evidence of direct fit includes knowledge of 'statistical metadata concepts and frameworks', 'methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata', and analysis of changes in methods and systems to determine where metadata and documentation updates are required. Its awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts also supports secure and compliant component design.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected because subprocess 3.2 concerns building or reusing operational processing components for repeated production, and this position works directly on manual and automated operations for collection, coding and processing of data. The subprocess requires capability to define, assess and improve operational processing methods, system requirements, testing specifications and production workflows, especially under drivers for orchestration, modular architecture, efficiency and secure processing. This work description satisfies that need through responsibilities to 'participate in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data', 'evaluate collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommend alternatives', and 'prepare reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems'. Strong evidence also appears in contextual knowledge of 'systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows' for 'designing the specifications for testing of applications, the application and conversion of databases, and the maintenance and use of databases both for regular production of statistical data and for ad hoc manipulations and retrievals'. The role's analysis of system requirements for 'developing new processing systems' directly aligns with building reusable processing components.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is highly relevant because subprocess 3.2 includes building or reusing analysis components as designed in the Design phase, and this position explicitly contributes to translating subject-matter and methodological requirements into system development specifications and improving processing methods. The subprocess needs capability to operationalize methodological innovation into processing and analysis components, assess impacts of changed methods and technologies, and propose alternative systems. This work description satisfies that need through liaison 'to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development', and through participation in analysis that suggests feedback on 'collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures'. Evidence also includes knowledge of 'statistical or economic theory and principles and the relevance of their application in a computerized environment', 'methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling', and research responsibilities to 'analyze current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems'. This directly supports reusable analytical and processing component development under drivers such as AI/automation, modern methods and modular architecture.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because subprocess 3.2 depends on processing specifications and system integration that affect downstream data production outputs, and this position reviews impacts of new or modified systems and processing specifications on data products. The subprocess requires capability to assess whether built or reused processing components produce valid, integrated and usable outputs. This work description satisfies that need by 'review[ing] and assess[ing] data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases' and by examining 'new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems'. It also includes liaison 'to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development'. While the role is more downstream in production/dissemination than direct component building, its responsibilities for assessing processing changes, adapting data to new definitions or formats, and ensuring consistency and reliability make it materially connected.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role has a limited but still material connection because subprocess 3.2 includes analysis components and data requirements that may need evaluation-oriented analytical support, but the position is not primarily responsible for building production processing components. The subprocess needs some capability to assess data requirements, analytical methods and implications of results, especially where new processing or analysis components support evaluation studies. This work description satisfies that need only indirectly through responsibilities to 'identify, gather, analyze and synthesize quantitative and qualitative data', 'apply analytical tools and techniques', and 'recommend... enhancements to methods for retrieving data'. It also supports assessment of 'current and future requirements for data' and analysis of databases. However, the role is centered on evaluation studies under supervision rather than on building reusable processing and analysis components, pipelines, metadata services or operational systems, so relevance is low.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is directly implicated because subprocess 3.3 is about building or reusing dissemination components, and metadata is a core dissemination component for discoverability, standards-based access, and reusable dissemination services. The subprocess explicitly includes dissemination outputs such as web services, open data and linked data, all of which depend on well-structured metadata. This role requires the capability to prepare, validate, store and disseminate metadata, translate client requirements into specifications, test new procedures and systems, and evaluate metadata quality. It satisfies the need created by drivers D004, D005, D006, D007, D009 and D011 because it supports repository-based dissemination, standards and discoverability, reusable methods, and compliant dissemination practices. Evidence includes: "Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository"; "Provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata; and participates in the testing of new procedures and systems"; "Liaises with other statistical metadata specialists... to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata"; and knowledge of "software used in the production, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata." The role also addresses secure dissemination context through awareness of the "Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information."

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is directly connected to subprocess 3.3 because it explicitly covers dissemination of statistical data and the adaptation of outputs for users, which is central to building or reusing dissemination components. The subprocess concerns components that deliver products through publications, web services, open data and other channels; this role supports those outputs by editing, validating, disseminating data, interpreting user requests, and adapting data to new presentation formats. The needed capability is operational responsibility for dissemination outputs, user-facing data services, custom tabulations, and assessing impacts of system and technology changes on products and services. This role satisfies those needs through direct dissemination work and through participation in system-related specification and improvement activities, aligning strongly with D004, D005, D007, D009 and D011, and also with D006 where dissemination depends on coherent output structures and user interpretation. Evidence includes: "Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data"; "Interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations"; "Provides statistical data and consultative services to users"; "Participates on data production and dissemination teams"; "Liaises with other specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development"; and "Adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats." Security and privacy requirements are also explicit: awareness of the "Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data."

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected because subprocess 3.3 includes building or reusing dissemination components for statistical products, and this position contributes to publication-oriented analytical material, presentation methods, and specification development that influence how dissemination components are designed and improved. The relevant subprocess aspect is the preparation and presentation of outputs for publication and the analysis of how procedural or technological changes affect products and services. The needed capability is subject-matter translation into system specifications, assessment of presentation methods, and analysis of impacts on outputs. This role satisfies that need through participation in analytical material for publication, liaison to translate requirements into system development specifications, and analysis of changes affecting data output, products and services. Evidence includes: "participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes"; "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development"; and "Analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services." It is less direct than the dissemination-specific roles because its primary focus is subject-matter analysis rather than dissemination component production.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because modern dissemination components under subprocess 3.3 are increasingly data-driven, automated, and platform-based, especially under drivers such as AI and Automation, Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and self-service dissemination. The relevant subprocess aspect is the preparation, transformation, validation and visualization of data that feed dissemination products and reusable dissemination services. The needed capability is data preparation to standards, quality assurance, visualization, and communication with users and specialists to translate requirements into specifications. This role satisfies that need through data extraction, cleansing, transformation, validation, conformity to standards, and preparation of reports, briefings and dashboards. Evidence includes: "Conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards"; knowledge of the data science life cycle including "reporting, visualization, business intelligence"; "Writing skills are necessary to draft clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools"; and "liaise with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development." It is medium relevance because it supports enabling data and analytical capabilities for dissemination components, but does not explicitly own dissemination component build/reuse.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role has a partial connection to subprocess 3.3 because dissemination components depend on operational systems, processing specifications, and publication-oriented outputs, but the position is primarily focused on collection, coding and processing rather than dissemination build. The relevant subprocess aspect is the operational and systems support needed when dissemination components reuse upstream automated processes or require integration with statistical processing systems. The needed capability is understanding system requirements, data flows, testing specifications, and preparation of publication-ready tables and charts. This role satisfies that need through operational systems analysis and some output preparation. Evidence includes: "Designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications"; "Prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems"; and contextual knowledge of "systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows... for designing the specifications for testing of applications." It is low relevance because dissemination components are not a primary responsibility, though some supporting capabilities are relevant.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is directly connected to configuring operational workflows for collection, coding and processing, which is the core of GSBPM 3.4. The subprocess requires capability to implement and maintain manual and automated operational flows, assess system requirements, define testing specifications, coordinate with subject matter and systems specialists, and embed secure and efficient operational procedures. This work description satisfies that need because it explicitly states the position 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' 'evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives,' and 'prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems.' It also includes workflow-relevant systems capability through 'knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows' and responsibility to 'assess and review system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems.' The security and governance drivers are also materially relevant because the role requires awareness of the 'Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially implicated because workflow configuration increasingly depends on metadata-driven processing, standards, repository loading, and quality controls, all of which are central to driver D006 and also support orchestration, reuse and governance. The subprocess requires capability to configure workflows so that metadata production, storage, dissemination and evaluation are built into end-to-end processes. This work description satisfies that need because it states the position 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository,' 'provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata; and participates in the testing of new procedures and systems,' and 'liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications.' It also directly supports workflow standardization and documentation through input to 'procedures manuals and training manuals' and analysis of 'changes in methods, procedures and systems used to produce, store, disseminate and evaluate the quality of statistical metadata.' Security and compliance are also relevant because the role requires awareness of the 'Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because configured workflows in 3.4 must operationalize data extraction, cleansing, transformation, validation and quality checks, especially under drivers for automation, integrated pipelines, administrative data and modern methods. The subprocess requires capability to define and support data preparation steps that can be embedded into automated or orchestrated pipelines. This work description satisfies that need through explicit responsibility for 'data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin.' It also includes communication needed for workflow configuration by 'discuss[ing] data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients or service providers to comprehend and elaborate the conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur' and by liaising 'to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development.' The knowledge base also aligns with pipeline configuration because it covers the data science life cycle including 'data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing' and includes data stewardship, protection and secure use.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is connected to workflow configuration because it contributes subject-matter and methodological requirements that must be translated into system and process specifications. GSBPM 3.4 requires workflows to be configured based on design and to accommodate changes in methods, processing and outputs. This work description satisfies that need because it states the position 'liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates.' It also includes analysis directly relevant to workflow redesign: 'analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services' and 'analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.' Security and policy controls are also relevant through required knowledge of the Statistics Act and Privacy Acts.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because configured workflows span through downstream production and dissemination, and this position assesses how revised processing specifications affect integration and coordination across systems. The subprocess requires capability to ensure configured workflows support data validation, production outputs, dissemination steps and interoperability with other divisional systems. This work description satisfies that need because it includes responsibility to 'review and assess data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases' and to 'examine operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems.' It also supports translation of requirements into system specifications by liaising 'with other specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development.' The role further aligns with governance and security drivers through knowledge of policies and awareness of the 'Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is directly implicated because the subprocess focuses on testing assembled production services, workflows, secure transmission arrangements, and readiness of operational routines before production. The role participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for collection, coding and processing of data, which is closely aligned with production-system testing. It explicitly includes capability for testing and operational validation through 'knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows... for designing the specifications for testing of applications, the application and conversion of databases, and the maintenance and use of databases both for regular production of statistical data and for ad hoc manipulations and retrievals.' The role also 'assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems,' which supports sign-off and readiness testing of new or modified production solutions. Drivers around integrated pipelines, cloud/platform change, reusable architecture, and governance are especially relevant because the role works across operational systems, data flows, procedures, and quality controls. Security and external-source testing are also implicated because the role 'contacts data suppliers or respondents... to clarify problems or irregularities' and must maintain awareness of the 'Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected because GSBPM 3.5 explicitly includes checking files and metadata, validating interoperability, and ensuring the assembled production solution works coherently end to end. The work description directly states that the position 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata,' 'provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata; and participates in the testing of new procedures and systems.' That is a direct testing responsibility. The subprocess need for metadata exchange, standards conformance, and linkage between data and metadata is satisfied by the role's 'knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks,' 'knowledge of methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata,' and analysis of 'changes in methods, procedures and systems... to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats.' Drivers on metadata standards, integrated pipelines, reusable architecture, and governance are strongly implicated because this role liaises with specialists and survey managers 'to develop and translate requirements into specifications' and evaluates metadata quality across programs. Security/privacy aspects are also relevant because the role must have 'awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because testing production systems increasingly requires validation of data extraction, transformation, validation, standards conformance, source integrity, and quality under automated and integrated workflows. The work description includes 'conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin,' which is directly relevant to testing whether production routines and incoming files are fit for use. The role also has knowledge of the 'data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing' and knowledge of 'data risk assessment' and protecting and securing data. These capabilities support subprocess needs arising from AI and automation, administrative and alternative data, integrated pipelines, and modern methods, especially where test data, source validity, and reproducibility must be checked. Relevance is medium rather than high because the description emphasizes analytical support and data preparation rather than explicit responsibility for end-to-end production-system testing, sign-off, or integration testing across assembled services.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected through its responsibility to assess impacts of changes in procedures, methods, and computer technology on outputs and to propose changes to collection and processing methods. GSBPM 3.5 includes confirming that routines and workflows operate coherently and produce reliable results in production conditions, especially under modern methods and integrated solutions. The work description states that the position 'liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development,' and in research and analysis it 'analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services' and 'analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.' These capabilities support testing of methodological coherence, output validity, and suitability of existing routines for reuse. Security/privacy and governance are also relevant through required knowledge of the Statistics Act and policies. Relevance is medium because the role contributes to assessing effects and requirements but does not explicitly own testing of systems, workflows, secure channels, or technical sign-off.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because the subprocess includes validating outputs from new or modified systems, checking integration with other divisional systems, and ensuring production readiness of data workflows. The work description explicitly states that the position 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases,' which is directly relevant to testing production systems. It also 'examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems.' That aligns strongly with drivers concerning integrated pipelines, reusable architecture, cloud/platform changes, and interoperability. The role's responsibilities for editing, validating and disseminating data, plus analyzing changes in procedures and computer technology, support the subprocess need to confirm that assembled solutions produce reliable outputs. Relevance is medium because the description is more focused on data quality and downstream production/dissemination impacts than on explicit technical testing, secure transmission testing, or formal sign-off of the whole production solution.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is directly connected to piloting and end-to-end testing of a statistical business process because the subprocess explicitly covers managing field tests or pilots, testing collection instruments, and validating processing under realistic operational conditions. The role’s relevant subprocess aspect is operational testing of collection, coding and processing workflows, including identifying problems and recommending adjustments after pilot results. The needed capability is responsibility for implementing and assessing operational procedures, testing applications and databases, evaluating collection/coding methods, and reporting operational issues. This work description satisfies that need because it 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' 'evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives,' and 'provides input to training materials concerning data collection operations and assists in training delivery,' which aligns with workforce-transition and pilot-readiness needs. It also contains explicit testing and systems evidence: 'knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows... for designing the specifications for testing of applications, the application and conversion of databases,' and research responsibilities to 'assess and review system requirements' and analyze 'problems encountered in implementing concepts, definitions, classifications and other instructions, and recommending alternatives.' Privacy and secure operations are also relevant through awareness of 'the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially implicated because subprocess 3.6 requires pilot data to be processed and analyzed to verify that the business process performs as expected, especially under AI, automation, integrated pipeline, and alternative-data drivers. The relevant subprocess aspect is testing data flows, data quality, transformations, validation, and analytical outputs from pilot runs. The needed capability is hands-on data preparation and analysis, assessment of data quality and integrity, understanding of data science lifecycle components, and communication with operational and systems stakeholders to refine requirements. This work description satisfies that need because it 'conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin' and 'supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods and software such as Python, SAS, STATA, R.' It also explicitly covers integrated pipeline concerns through knowledge of 'data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing, mining... reporting, visualization,' and quality/risk concerns through 'knowledge of techniques and methods of information collection and analysis... data risk assessment... in order to assess the quality of data and identify and mitigate risks to its integrity.' Communication evidence also supports pilot coordination: the role 'discusses data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists' and liaises to translate requirements into specifications.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is strongly connected to testing a statistical business process because pilots require analysis of collected and processed pilot data, assessment of methodological performance, and recommendations for changes to collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods. The relevant subprocess aspect is evaluating whether methods and outputs perform as intended and determining what should be adjusted before full deployment. The needed capability is subject-matter and methodological analysis across the statistical production chain, including feasibility and impact assessment of modified programs and methods. This work description satisfies that need because it 'participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.' It also includes knowledge of 'methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs' and research responsibilities to 'analyze current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.' This directly supports drivers related to methodological innovation, integrated processes, and iterative pilot refinement. Security/privacy relevance is also present through required awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because pilot testing of a statistical business process includes validating outputs from new or modified systems and databases and ensuring resulting data products are consistent, reliable and fit for use. The relevant subprocess aspect is downstream validation of pilot outputs and assessing effects of revised processing specifications on integrated functions. The needed capability is reviewing data quality from changed systems, analyzing consistency and reliability, and examining integration impacts across data capture and processing functions. This work description satisfies that need because it 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases' and 'edits, validates... and disseminates data.' Its research responsibilities are especially relevant to integrated pipeline and orchestration drivers: it 'examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems,' and 'analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.' It also supports workforce-transition aspects through drafting manuals and training packages. Relevance is medium rather than high because the role is more focused on output validation and dissemination than on managing the pilot itself.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected because testing a statistical business process under modern, modular, and integrated architectures requires validating that metadata, documentation, standards and repository loading work correctly across the pilot process. The relevant subprocess aspect is testing supporting metadata procedures and systems that enable collection, processing, certification, dissemination and auditability. The needed capability is participation in testing new procedures and systems, evaluating metadata quality, translating requirements into specifications, and ensuring compliance with standards and privacy obligations. This work description satisfies that need because it 'provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata; and participates in the testing of new procedures and systems.' It also includes knowledge of 'survey and statistical program subject matter concepts and methodologies relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data' and analysis of 'current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives.' This is relevant to integrated pipelines, reusable architecture, and governance/auditability drivers. Privacy and secure handling are also evidenced by awareness of 'the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information.' Relevance is medium because the role supports an important enabling layer of the pilot rather than the full business-process pilot itself.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role has a weaker but still material connection because subprocess 3.6 involves assessing pilot performance and deciding whether adjustments are needed before deployment. The relevant subprocess aspect is evaluation of pilot results, evidence gathering, and synthesis of findings for decision-making and governance. The needed capability is structured research, qualitative and quantitative evidence collection, analysis, and reporting to management on performance and implications. This work description satisfies that need because it 'undertakes assigned tasks related to specific elements of evaluation projects such as... identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data' and 'provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions.' It also supports governance and execution-discipline drivers through providing 'supporting data for sections of reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda for senior management' and attending meetings 'to discuss files / issues and evaluation requirements.' Relevance is low because the role is oriented to program evaluation rather than direct testing of statistical collection, processing systems, methods, or operational workflows.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is directly connected to finalising production systems because the subprocess focuses on moving configured processes into production, documenting them, ensuring they work in the production environment, and training users. The relevant subprocess aspects are operational implementation, production readiness, procedures, monitoring, and user training. The capability needed is responsibility for implementing and maintaining manual and automated operations, preparing operational documentation, assessing system requirements, and supporting users in live operational contexts. This work description satisfies that need because it explicitly states the position 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' 'provides assistance and advice to users on methods and practices of collection and coding,' and 'provides input to training materials concerning data collection operations and assists in training delivery.' It also includes production-oriented documentation and deployment support through evidence such as 'writes survey information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports,' 'prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems,' and 'assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems.' The role is further strengthened by contextual knowledge of 'systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows' and awareness of the 'Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data,' which aligns with secure deployment, governed operations, and production controls under the listed drivers.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected to finalising production systems because the subprocess explicitly includes producing technical documentation and user manuals, training users, and ensuring production-ready operation, while the drivers emphasize metadata standards, discoverability, governance, and operational documentation. The relevant subprocess aspect is the documentation and operationalization of production services, especially where metadata standards and repository loading are part of readiness. The capability needed is to prepare and validate metadata for production use, update procedures and training materials when methods or systems change, assist clients, and support testing and quality evaluation. This work description satisfies that need because it states the position 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository,' 'provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata; and participates in the testing of new procedures and systems,' and 'provides input to documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals related to the production and dissemination of statistical metadata and assists with the delivery of training.' It also directly addresses production change impacts through evidence that the role 'analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems used to produce, store, disseminate and evaluate the quality of statistical metadata in order to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats and to determine where updates are required to existing documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals.' Its knowledge of policies, directives, repository practices, and awareness of the 'Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information' aligns strongly with governance, secure access, discoverability, and controlled production deployment.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is connected to finalising production systems because the subprocess includes preparing systems and outputs for operational use, documenting procedures, supporting users, and training staff. The relevant subprocess aspect is readiness of data products and supporting operational materials once systems or databases are new or modified. The capability needed is to assess impacts of changed systems on outputs, support users, and contribute manuals and training packages that help operational staff use production systems correctly. This work description satisfies that need because it states the position 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases,' 'provides statistical data and consultative services to users,' and 'provides input to training material and assists in the delivery.' It also includes documentation and system-integration evidence: 'drafts program information manuals and training packages for use by colleagues, operational staff and management, and assists in the delivery of training,' and 'examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems.' This makes the role relevant to production finalisation, especially where deployment affects downstream data products and user adoption, though it is less directly focused on deployment operations than the Operations Officer.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because finalising production systems requires translating subject-matter requirements into operational specifications, documenting procedures, and assessing how changes in methods, technology, and services affect outputs in production. The relevant subprocess aspect is ensuring that production-ready systems and procedures remain fit for purpose and understandable to operational staff and users. The capability needed is subject-matter translation into system specifications, preparation of manuals and training packages, and analysis of impacts from procedural or technology changes. This work description satisfies that need because it states the position 'liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development,' and 'writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports for use by colleagues, operational staff and management in the development, implementation and assessment of statistical programs.' It also includes production-change analysis through evidence that the role 'analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services' and 'analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.' This supports production readiness and controlled implementation, although the role is more subject-matter and analytical than operational deployment-focused.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role has a lower but still material connection to finalising production systems because some drivers emphasize integrated pipelines, automation, governance, and secure handling of data in operational environments. The relevant subprocess aspect is preparing data workflows and understanding operational conditions for statistical development and operations. The capability needed is data preparation, validation, standards conformance, communication with operations and systems specialists, and awareness of governance and secure handling requirements. This work description satisfies that need through evidence that the position 'conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin,' and 'discusses data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients or service providers to comprehend and elaborate the conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur.' It also includes governance and security-related capability: 'provides advice, information and guidance to data users and clients regarding governance concepts used to protect and optimize the utility of Statistics Canada’s data assets' and requires 'basic knowledge of Departmental, Central Agencies and Library and Archives Canada policies pertaining to the handling, tracking, filing and storing of sensitive and confidential material and information holdings.' However, the role does not explicitly emphasize deployment, production documentation, or user training, so relevance is lower.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is materially connected because subprocess 4.1 requires constructing frames from available sources, assessing whether sampling is needed, and using auxiliary information to improve sample design. The role explicitly supports data preparation activities such as "data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin," which are directly relevant to creating usable frames from administrative and alternative data. The subprocess also requires methodological capability for sample design and quality assessment; this role requires "knowledge of techniques and methods of information collection and analysis, evolving information sources, survey methodologies, data risk assessment, impact and quantitative analysis" and also "basic knowledge... including... statistical sampling." Those capabilities align strongly with the drivers on administrative data and modern statistical methods. The role also communicates with operational and subject matter staff to define conditions for statistical operations, evidenced by "discusss data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists" and "liaise with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development," which supports implementation of efficient, coordinated frame and sample processes.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is strongly implicated because subprocess 4.1 is an operational production activity involving implementation, evaluation, coordination and quality assurance of collection frames and selected samples. The position "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection... of data" and "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," which is directly relevant to operationalizing frame creation and sample selection procedures. The subprocess also emphasizes overlap management, burden reduction and approval/quality assurance; this role brings the needed operational control capability through "knowledge of the concepts, methods and techniques used in the management and control of statistical collection... activities" and "knowledge of methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications." It also analyzes source changes and system requirements, matching the drivers around administrative data and efficiency: "Analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results" and "assesses and reviews system requirements". Its interaction with subject matter specialists, clients and service providers to understand operational conditions further supports coordinated and efficient sample implementation.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is highly relevant because subprocess 4.1 depends on methodological understanding of survey universes, data gathering, estimation and the effects of collection conditions on outputs. The role includes "knowledge of statistical or economic theory and principles... and the methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation" and "knowledge of the subject and universe of the survey is required in order to propose suitable changes to statistical or reporting methods and techniques." That directly supports frame definition and sample selection decisions. The subprocess also requires adapting methods in response to modern statistical methods and auxiliary data; this role explicitly "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems" and "assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored." Those responsibilities align with evaluating improved frames, coordination rules and efficient sample approaches. Its liaison role in translating subject-matter requirements into specifications also supports implementation of frame and sample designs in production.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated at a moderate level because subprocess 4.1 includes quality assurance and assessment of data sources and system changes that affect frame creation and sample implementation, though the role is more downstream than directly sample-focused. It "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases" and "compiles data from diverse sources" while "analyz[ing] and evaluat[ing] data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness." These capabilities are relevant where administrative and alternative data are used to instantiate frames or provide auxiliary variables. The role also "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems," which connects to coordination and efficiency drivers in sample operations. However, the description does not explicitly mention frame construction or sample selection, so relevance is medium rather than high.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is moderately relevant because subprocess 4.1 depends on clear metadata, standards, and quality evaluation for frames, auxiliary variables, source integration and sample-related procedures, especially under increased use of administrative and alternative data. The position "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," provides advice on "documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines," and participates in "statistical metadata quality evaluations." These responsibilities support the need to document frame definitions, source provenance, variable usage and methodological changes. The role also has "knowledge of survey and statistical program subject matter concepts and methodologies relevant to the collection... of data" and "analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives," which aligns with modernization and quality assurance aspects of the subprocess. It is less directly responsible for selecting samples, so medium relevance is appropriate.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role has a limited but still material connection because subprocess 4.1 is influenced by decisions about data sources, methods and efficiency, and the role contributes to assessing data requirements and source usefulness. Evidence includes "provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data; gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases" and "identifies and recommends... the usefulness and accessible sources of data to be used in studies." Those capabilities can inform whether administrative or alternative data can support frame creation or reduce the need for sampling. The role also has knowledge of statistics and research methods and participates in quantitative and qualitative analysis. However, the work description is centered on program evaluation studies rather than statistical production operations, and it does not explicitly address frame construction, sample coordination or sample selection. Therefore relevance is low.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is directly aligned to setting up collection because the subprocess is about ensuring collection people, processes and technology are operationally ready, including training staff, configuring systems, preparing instruments, coordinating with suppliers/respondents, and maintaining secure collection operations. The role’s relevant subprocess aspects include implementation and maintenance of manual and automated collection operations, evaluation of collection methods and procedures, operational coordination with subject matter specialists, systems specialists, clients and service providers, and preparation of training and operational documentation. The capability needed is operational readiness for collection environments, including collection-system/process setup, method evaluation, stakeholder coordination, respondent/supplier interaction, and training support under changing digital, automated and secure collection models. This role satisfies that need because it explicitly 'Participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' 'Evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives,' 'Provides assistance and advice to users on methods and practices of collection and coding,' and 'Provides input to training materials concerning data collection operations and assists in training delivery.' It also contains strong evidence for digital and integrated setup needs through 'Knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows' and 'Assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems.' It is materially connected to administrative/alternative data and supplier setup because it 'Contacts data suppliers or respondents to obtain their collaboration... explain technical procedures for obtaining the data in the appropriate format.' It is materially connected to cybersecurity/privacy because it requires awareness of 'the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially implicated because collection setup explicitly includes readiness to receive data and metadata, use agreed formats, maintain inventories/documentation, and support discoverability and standardized operational arrangements. The relevant subprocess aspects are configuring collection arrangements so metadata can be captured, stored and disseminated correctly; documenting procedures; supporting training; and ensuring compliance and metadata quality across programs. The capability needed is expertise in statistical metadata standards, repositories, procedures, system testing, documentation and liaison with survey managers and subject matter specialists so collection channels and processes are metadata-ready. This work description satisfies that need because it 'Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository,' 'provides assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines,' and 'participates in the testing of new procedures and systems.' It also directly supports setup/training requirements because it 'Provides input to documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals... and assists with the delivery of training.' Evidence of direct relevance to collection operations appears in the knowledge requirement for 'survey and statistical program subject matter concepts and methodologies relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data' and in liaison responsibilities to 'develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.' It is also connected to security/confidentiality setup through awareness of the 'Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because several drivers shift collection setup toward automated acquisition, extraction, validation, standards conformance, and coordination with collection operations managers and service providers. The relevant subprocess aspects are readiness of APIs and digital channels, extraction/prefill-type workflows, validation of incoming data, and support for more automated and alternative-data collection arrangements. The capability needed is data lifecycle and acquisition expertise, including extraction, transformation, validation, standards conformance, data risk assessment, and communication with operational and technical stakeholders. This work description satisfies that need because it 'Conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin.' It also explicitly supports collection setup coordination because, 'As assigned, discusses data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients or service providers to comprehend and elaborate the conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur.' The role’s knowledge base is relevant to AI/automation and integrated pipelines because it includes 'data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing' and knowledge of 'survey methodologies, data risk assessment' as well as protecting and securing data. It is not as directly collection-setup-focused as Operations Officer, but it materially supports the technical readiness dimensions of the subprocess.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because collection setup includes adapting methods, procedures, training materials and system specifications in response to methodological and operational changes, and this position explicitly analyzes and proposes changes to collection-related methods and procedures. The relevant subprocess aspects are planning and readiness for collection under changing concepts, definitions, technologies and respondent/program contexts. The capability needed is subject-matter and methodological analysis to assess whether collection methods, procedures and system specifications remain relevant and to translate requirements into operational changes. This work description satisfies that need because it 'participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.' It also supports setup through communication responsibilities that 'develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development' and through writing 'program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports.' Research evidence is especially relevant: it 'Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems' and 'Analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.' Security/confidentiality awareness is also present through required knowledge of the Statistics and Privacy Acts.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is only indirectly implicated. The subprocess is primarily about preparing collection operations before data capture begins, whereas this position is centered on editing, validation, dissemination and custom tabulations after or adjacent to capture. However, some responsibilities connect materially to setup drivers involving system changes, integration and training. The relevant subprocess aspects are assessing impacts of new or revised processing specifications on data capture/processing integration, supporting training materials, and ensuring secure handling of data in evolving systems. The capability needed is understanding how revised system concepts and processing specifications affect upstream data capture and coordinated operations. This work description satisfies that limited need because it 'Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases,' 'Provides input to training material and assists in the delivery,' and 'Examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems.' It also includes confidentiality awareness under the Statistics and Privacy Acts. Relevance remains low because the core duties focus on post-collection data production and dissemination rather than direct setup of collection staff, instruments, channels or supplier arrangements.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is directly aligned to GSBPM 4.3 because the subprocess is the live execution and monitoring of collection, including respondent/supplier contact, follow-up, operational control, basic intake checks, reporting, and adjustments to improve quality. The role’s relevant subprocess aspects are explicit: it “participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,” “evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives,” and “participates on data collection and operations teams.” The subprocess needs capability for running collection channels, managing contacts with respondents or suppliers, monitoring operations, producing manuals and reports, and adapting procedures in response to issues and efficiency pressures. This role satisfies that need through responsibilities such as “contacts data suppliers or respondents to obtain their collaboration in responding to surveys, to clarify problems or irregularities,” including explaining “technical procedures for obtaining the data in the appropriate format,” which matches collection follow-up and intake integrity checks. It also supports operational monitoring and adaptive intervention through “writes survey information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports” and “analyses reported data and work results and prepares reports... presenting findings on how the survey was conducted, problems encountered... and recommending alternatives.” The drivers are strongly reflected: AI/automation and orchestration through “manual and automated operations”; administrative and alternative data through contact with “data suppliers”; metadata/data standards through obtaining data “in the appropriate format”; cybersecurity/privacy through awareness of “the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data”; workforce transformation through training materials and delivery; and efficiency/methodological adaptation through evaluating methods and recommending alternatives.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected because GSBPM 4.3 includes machine-to-machine acquisition, scheduled transfers, monitoring of incoming data, basic structural checks, and routing data into downstream processes. The relevant subprocess aspect is the operational handling of incoming data and associated quality/conformance checks during collection execution. The subprocess needs capability in data capture/acquisition, validation, conformity to standards, data origin assessment, liaison with collection operations, and support for dashboards or monitoring. This work description satisfies that need through key activities such as “conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin.” It also explicitly connects to collection operations by stating that, as assigned, the incumbent “discusses data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients or service providers.” The knowledge requirements strongly match the drivers affecting run collection: “knowledge of data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing... reporting, visualization, business intelligence” supports integrated pipelines, automated acquisition, and monitoring dashboards; “knowledge of techniques and methods of information collection and analysis... survey methodologies, data risk assessment” supports adaptive collection and quality monitoring; and “data stewardship... assess the quality of data, protect and secure data” supports secure handling during collection. This role is therefore highly implicated where collection is increasingly automated, supplier-driven, standards-based, and monitored in near real time.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because GSBPM 4.3 explicitly includes collecting associated metadata and ensuring incoming files or feeds conform to expected structures that support downstream integration. The relevant subprocess aspect is metadata capture, validation, standardization, and quality support during collection execution. The subprocess needs capability to prepare and validate metadata, translate requirements into metadata specifications, assess metadata quality, and support standard structures for incoming data and metadata. This work description satisfies that need through key activities such as “prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository,” and “provides assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines.” It also supports collection-related integration and standards through communication responsibilities to “develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata” and research responsibilities that “analyze changes in methods, procedures and systems... to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats.” Evidence also shows direct relevance to collection context: knowledge of “survey and statistical program subject matter concepts and methodologies relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data” and awareness of privacy/security obligations. Relevance is medium rather than high because the role is not primarily responsible for live respondent/supplier contact or fieldwork execution, but it is materially connected through metadata standards, discoverability, and downstream-ready collection intake.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated through the adaptive and methodological dimensions of GSBPM 4.3, especially where collection is monitored and adjusted based on response patterns, paradata, and operational results. The relevant subprocess aspect is feedback on collection methods and analysis of how collection conditions affect data quality and outputs. The subprocess needs capability to assess collection procedures, understand respondent and program context, and recommend improvements to methods and operations. This work description satisfies that need because it “participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.” Its research responsibilities further align with adaptive collection and methodological innovation: it “assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected” and “analyzes current collection... methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.” Contextual knowledge of “program sponsors, participants and respondents” and legal/privacy obligations also supports collection operations. Relevance is medium because the role influences and evaluates collection execution rather than directly running collection channels or managing live operational contacts.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role has a secondary connection to GSBPM 4.3 through intake quality, data capture integration, and the effects of revised processing specifications on collection-related functions. The relevant subprocess aspect is the basic checking of incoming data and the coordination between data capture and downstream processing once collection is running. The subprocess needs capability to assess whether incoming data are valid, consistent, and compatible with operational systems and downstream use. This work description satisfies that need through activities such as “reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases” and research responsibilities that “examine operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems.” It also “compiles data from diverse sources” and “analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness,” which is relevant to basic structural and integrity checks on collected data. Relevance is low because the role is centered on editing, validation, custom tabulation, and dissemination after collection rather than on executing collection itself, but it remains materially connected where collection feeds are integrated into production systems.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is only indirectly implicated. The relevant subprocess aspect is limited to gathering information from multiple sources and communicating with clients during acquisition activities, which can inform understanding of collection requirements and performance. The subprocess needs some capability to identify data requirements, gather information from varied sources, and maintain positive stakeholder interactions. This work description satisfies that need in a limited way because it “provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data; gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases,” and communication evidence states the incumbent is “required to communicate with clients in the data acquisition process.” It also “collects diverse data and information from a variety of sources.” However, the role is primarily focused on evaluation studies rather than operational statistical collection, respondent follow-up, supplier transfer management, intake monitoring, or collection system execution. Therefore it is materially connected only at the margins and has low relevance.
