implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is directly connected to finalising collection because the subprocess covers loading collected data and metadata into processing environments, handling manual and automated capture, format handling, and ensuring collection outputs are ready for downstream processing. The work description explicitly states the position 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' which aligns closely with automated and manual capture and operational handoff. The subprocess also requires evaluation of collection results, metadata/paradata readiness, and controlled transition into processing systems; this role 'evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives' and 'prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems.' Capabilities needed include operational knowledge of collection-processing workflows, data verification, system/data-flow understanding, and secure handling. The description provides this through 'knowledge of the concepts, methods and techniques used in the management and control of statistical collection, coding and processing activities,' 'knowledge of methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications,' and 'knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows... for designing the specifications for testing of applications, the application and conversion of databases.' It is also materially relevant to drivers around pipelines, automation, external formats, cloud/platform operations, and privacy because it addresses database conversion, system requirements, and confidentiality: 'application and conversion of databases' and awareness of the 'Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is strongly implicated because finalising collection explicitly includes loading metadata, analyzing metadata/paradata, versioning, archiving, and ensuring traceable handoff into further processing. The work description directly states that the position 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository.' That is a direct match to the subprocess requirement to load metadata into a suitable electronic environment. The subprocess also depends on metadata standards, documentation, discoverability, and version-aware processing; this role provides the needed capability through 'knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks,' 'knowledge of methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata,' and participation in 'testing of new procedures and systems.' It also supports transformation drivers around integrated pipelines, standards, reusable architecture, and cloud repositories because it 'provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata' and 'analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems... to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats.' Security and compliance are also relevant to finalisation and archiving, and the description explicitly notes 'awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected because finalising collection includes loading collected data, converting formats, encoding variables, validating readiness for downstream processing, and potentially pseudonymising data before further processing. The work description directly covers these needs: the position 'conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin.' These are core activities of finalising collection after acquisition and before processing. The subprocess is also shaped by automation, integrated pipelines, administrative/alternative data, and efficiency drivers; this role supports those through knowledge of the 'data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing' and through communication with 'operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients or service providers' to elaborate operational conditions. Capabilities needed include handling diverse incoming data, validating and transforming it to standards, assessing quality and provenance, and protecting sensitive data. The description explicitly includes 'data stewardship,' the ability to 'assess the quality of data, protect and secure data, and safeguard their responsible use,' as well as 'basic knowledge of... policies pertaining to the handling, tracking, filing and storing of sensitive and confidential material and information holdings, including electronic records.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is relevant because finalising collection requires validation of collected data, assessing outputs from systems and databases, and understanding how capture and processing functions integrate with downstream systems. The work description includes 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data' and 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases,' which aligns with the subprocess need to ensure collected data is properly loaded and suitable for further processing. It also addresses integration concerns central to pipeline and orchestration drivers: the role 'examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems.' Capabilities needed include data validation, adaptation to new formats, and understanding system impacts; the description supports this through 'analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness' and 'adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats.' It is somewhat less direct than collection-operations or metadata roles because its emphasis is broader production/dissemination rather than the collection-finalisation step itself.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated at a moderate level because finalising collection includes assessing whether collection outputs, metadata/paradata, and stored data meet requirements before downstream processing. The work description includes participation in feedback on 'collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures' and explicitly states that the position 'analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.' That analytical responsibility is relevant to evaluating whether finalised collection outputs are fit for processing and whether methods should change under automation and pipeline drivers. The subprocess also requires understanding the conditions under which data was collected and stored; this role provides that through 'assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored.' Privacy and policy awareness also align with secure handoff and controlled environments, as the description cites awareness of the 'Statistics and Privacy Acts.' Relevance is medium because the role is more focused on analytical review and methodological feedback than on direct operational loading, conversion, archiving, or metadata handling.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is directly connected to integrating data because the subprocess requires combining, transforming, validating and consolidating data from multiple sources into a coherent dataset. The subprocess is especially affected by automation, integrated pipelines, alternative data, and reusable tooling, all of which require practical capability in data preparation and data lifecycle activities. This position provides that capability through explicit responsibility for "data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin," which are core integration tasks. It also requires knowledge of the broader data science lifecycle including "data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing" and knowledge of evolving information sources, data risk assessment, and protecting and securing data. The communication requirements also support integration work because the role "discusses data requirements with operations managers... subject matter and systems specialists" and liaises to translate requirements into specifications for data development.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially implicated because successful data integration depends on interoperable metadata, standards, common concepts, and discoverability across sources. The subprocess description explicitly emphasizes harmonisation and combining data from multiple internal and external sources, which requires metadata frameworks and standardization. This position supplies that capability by preparing, editing, validating and disseminating statistical metadata and ensuring it is loaded to the corporate metadata repository. It also provides advice on "statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines" and participates in methods and systems for producing, storing and evaluating metadata. Evidence of direct relevance includes knowledge of "statistical metadata concepts and frameworks," knowledge of "survey and statistical program subject matter concepts and methodologies relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data," and analysis of changes in methods and systems to determine where metadata must be updated or adapted to new formats. Its awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts also supports the privacy-sensitive aspects of integrated data environments.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is strongly connected to data integration because the subprocess sits within processing and depends on operational data flows, processing systems, source changes, and secure handling of data. The position participates in "manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data" and evaluates methods, procedures and results, which is relevant where multiple sources must be ingested and coordinated in reproducible workflows. The capability needed for the subprocess includes understanding data flows, processing specifications, source changes, and system requirements for integrating data from different origins. This role satisfies that need through contextual knowledge of "systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows" for "the application and conversion of databases" and maintenance and use of databases for production and ad hoc retrievals. It also analyzes "changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results" and assesses system requirements for new processing systems. Its explicit awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts is also relevant to integration involving identifiers, confidentiality and secure handling.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because data integration is not only technical but also methodological: integrated data must be assessed for coherence, validity, consistency and the effects of differing concepts, definitions and collection conditions. The subprocess includes harmonising figures across sources and prioritising conflicting values, which requires subject-matter and methodological judgment. This position provides that through participation in analysis of statistical program data and feedback on "collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures." Evidence includes knowledge of "methods and techniques of data gathering," and socio-economic concepts and methods "to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data." It also "assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored" and analyzes current methods to propose alternatives. These responsibilities align with harmonisation and methodological integration, though the role is less explicitly operational than data-focused integration roles.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected because integrated data must be validated, assessed for quality, adapted across definitions and sources, and coordinated with processing systems before downstream use and dissemination. The subprocess requires consolidated data that may come from multiple sources and may need harmonisation or prioritisation. This position supports that need by editing and validating data, reviewing data quality from new and modified systems and databases, and compiling data from diverse sources. Strong evidence is the responsibility to "compile data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output" and to "analyze and evaluate data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness." It also "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems" and "adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats, depending on the complexity of the subject matter or the number of different sources." These are directly relevant to integrated data outputs, though the role appears somewhat more downstream than primary integration roles.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role has some connection to the subprocess because it gathers, analyzes and synthesizes quantitative and qualitative data from a variety of sources, which can involve combining information for evaluation purposes. The subprocess need here is limited to multi-source data use and interpretation rather than operational statistical data integration. The role satisfies this need in a supporting way through responsibilities to "identify, gather, analyze and synthesize quantitative and qualitative data," "gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases," and "collects diverse data and information from a variety of sources." It also recommends enhancements to methods for retrieving data. However, the work description is oriented to evaluation studies rather than production integration, record linkage, harmonisation pipelines, metadata interoperability, or secure identifier handling in statistical processing. Therefore the connection is real but limited.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is directly implicated because the subprocess is specifically about classifying and coding input data, and this position explicitly performs and supports those functions. The relevant aspect of the subprocess is the operational execution and improvement of coding activities, including both manual and automated coding within statistical production. The capability needed is responsibility for coding operations, evaluation of coding methods and results, support to users on coding practices, and understanding of data flows, system requirements, and quality controls. This position satisfies that need because its key activities include: "Participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "Evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," and "Provides assistance and advice to users on methods and practices of collection and coding." It also aligns strongly with the drivers around automation, pipelines, standards, efficiency, and skills transition through evidence such as knowledge of "the concepts, methods and techniques used in the management and control of statistical collection, coding and processing activities," knowledge of "methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications," and contextual knowledge of "systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows" for testing applications, database conversion, and production processing.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is materially connected because classify-and-code work depends heavily on data preparation, transformation, standards conformance, and increasingly automated and AI-enabled techniques. The relevant aspect of the subprocess is preparing input data for coding, transforming and validating coded outputs, and applying analytical and text-based methods that support automated classification. The capability needed is technical data processing skill, knowledge of the data science lifecycle, use of analytical software, and ability to assess quality and conformity to standards. This position satisfies that need because its key activities include "Conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin" and "Supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods and software such as Python, SAS, STATA, R, E-Views, SPSS or other similar software." It is especially relevant to drivers such as AI and Automation, Administrative and Alternative Data, Open-Source Enablement, and Methodological Innovation because the knowledge requirements explicitly include "data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization... text mining," as well as assessing data quality, integrity, stewardship, and governance.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is highly implicated because classify-and-code depends on approved classifications, code lists, metadata consistency, and machine-readable standards. The relevant aspect of the subprocess is the use and maintenance of statistical metadata that define and govern classifications, coding structures, and standardized outputs. The capability needed is expertise in statistical metadata concepts, standards, repositories, quality evaluation, and translating client requirements into metadata specifications. This position satisfies that need because its key activities include "Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository," "provides assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines," and "participates in the testing of new procedures and systems." This directly supports the Metadata, Data Standards and Discoverability driver. Supporting evidence includes knowledge of "statistical metadata concepts and frameworks... and how those concepts and frameworks are used and reflected in policies, methods and procedures relating to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata," knowledge of "survey and statistical program subject matter concepts and methodologies relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data," and analysis of changes in methods and systems to determine where metadata must be updated or adapted to new formats.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is implicated because classify-and-code is part of broader statistical processing, and this position contributes to assessing and improving processing methods, concepts, definitions, and data validity. The relevant aspect of the subprocess is methodological and subject-matter oversight of how coding and classification choices affect processed data quality, consistency, and downstream outputs. The capability needed is understanding of statistical concepts, data gathering and processing methods, and the ability to analyze impacts of changes in procedures and systems. This position satisfies that need because its key activities include participating in analysis of data and suggesting feedback on "collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures," and assisting in recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities. Evidence also includes knowledge of "the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data," and research responsibilities such as "Assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored" and "Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems." It is less direct than Operations Officer because coding is not explicitly assigned as a core duty, but it is materially connected through method and processing improvement.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is materially connected because classify-and-code outputs feed directly into edited, validated, and disseminated data products, and this role reviews effects of processing specifications and adapts data to new definitions and formats. The relevant aspect of the subprocess is ensuring coded data are valid, integrated with processing systems, and usable in standardized outputs and custom tabulations. The capability needed is validation of processed data, assessment of system and specification changes, and adaptation of data to revised definitions or formats. This position satisfies that need because its key activities include "Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data," "Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," and "Interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations." Supporting evidence includes research and analysis responsibilities to "Examine operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems" and to "Adapt data to new definitions or presentation formats." This aligns with drivers concerning pipelines, standards, and efficiency, though the role is more downstream from coding than directly responsible for coding itself.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description has a limited but still material connection because classify-and-code changes driven by automation, standards, and new data sources may need evaluation support through data gathering, analysis, and assessment of methods. The relevant aspect of the subprocess is not operational coding itself, but evaluation of data-related methods, requirements, and implications of process changes. The capability needed is ability to research data sources, analyze quantitative and qualitative information, and provide input on methods for retrieving and using data. This position satisfies that need through activities such as "identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data," "Provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data; gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases," and "Recommends... enhancements to methods for retrieving data as well as information used in the conduct of socio-economic analyses and cost-benefit analyses." However, there is no explicit responsibility for classification systems, coding operations, metadata standards, or automated coding routines, so the connection is indirect.

This position satisfies that need because its key activities include 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data' and 'Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases.' Its research and analysis responsibilities include 'Analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness,' and 'Examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems.' It also requires awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts, which is relevant to secure validation and controlled review of sensitive records.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected because the subprocess occurs within statistical processing operations and often depends on operational controls, verification methods, exception handling and interaction with collection and coding processes. The relevant subprocess aspect is operational validation of incoming data, verification against specifications, identification of irregularities, and adaptation of processing systems when source structures or workflows change. The needed capability is to implement and maintain manual and automated processing operations, verify data reliability and consistency, analyze impacts of source and system changes, and clarify irregularities with suppliers or respondents. This position satisfies that need because its key activities include 'Participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data' and 'Evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives.' Its knowledge requirements explicitly include 'Knowledge of methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications.' Its contextual and analytical evidence also aligns strongly: it requires knowledge of 'computer processing and data flows' for testing and database conversion, 'Analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results,' and it 'Contacts data suppliers or respondents to... clarify problems or irregularities.' This is highly relevant to iterative validation, exception routing and operational quality control.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because the subprocess increasingly depends on metadata-driven validation rules, structural conformance checks, standard definitions and interoperable pipelines. The relevant subprocess aspect is not direct record-level validation of survey or administrative data, but the metadata foundations that enable validation rules, standardization, quality evaluation and discoverability across systems. The needed capability is to prepare and validate metadata, assess metadata quality, interpret requirements into specifications, and support procedures and systems that govern how validation rules and structures are applied consistently. This position satisfies that need because its key activities include 'Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata' and 'assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations.' Its knowledge requirements explicitly mention 'statistical metadata concepts and frameworks' and 'methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata.' Its research and analysis responsibilities include 'Evaluates selected indicators of statistical metadata quality across survey and statistical programs in accordance with pre-defined quality guidelines' and 'Analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives.' This makes it materially relevant to metadata-driven validation under drivers D006 and D002, though less directly involved in validating input records themselves.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because review and validate requires analytical judgment about whether collected and processed data are valid, consistent and fit for use, especially when methods, concepts, sources or systems change. The relevant subprocess aspect is assessment of validity of processed data and outputs, feedback on editing and processing methods, and analysis of how methodological or contextual changes affect data quality. The needed capability is subject-matter and methodological analysis to assess validity, compare outputs, and recommend changes to collection, processing and editing procedures. This position satisfies that need because its key activities include participating in analysis and 'suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures.' Its knowledge requirements include 'Knowledge of the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data.' Its research and analysis section further states that it 'Assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored' and 'Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.' This is materially connected to validation, though less operationally direct than roles explicitly performing validation.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is directly connected to subprocess 5.4 because edit and impute depends on preparing, cleansing, transforming, validating and assessing the quality of data before corrected or replacement values can be inserted. The subprocess requires capability in identifying incorrect, missing or unreliable data, applying methods to change values, and increasingly doing so through automated and reproducible analytical tools. This work description satisfies that need through explicit responsibility for 'data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin.' It also requires knowledge of the full 'data science and its life cycle, including ... cleansing, processing, mining, clustering, modeling' and knowledge of statistical software such as 'Python, SAS, STATA, R,' which materially supports AI/automation, open-source implementation, and reusable processing routines. Its knowledge of 'survey methodologies, data risk assessment' and ability to 'assess the quality of data and identify and mitigate risks to its integrity' is directly relevant to determining when edits or imputations are needed, especially for administrative and alternative data.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially implicated because edit and impute sits within statistical processing operations and requires controlled manual and automated procedures, verification of data, and adaptation of processing systems when data issues are detected. The subprocess needs operational responsibility for implementing and maintaining processing workflows, evaluating methods, and ensuring reliable execution in integrated pipelines. This work description directly covers 'implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data' and 'evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives.' It also explicitly requires 'knowledge of methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications,' which is central to editing. The contextual knowledge of 'systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows' and research activity that 'assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems' aligns strongly with drivers around integrated pipelines, orchestration, automation, efficiency and platform-based processing.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is directly implicated because the work description explicitly includes editing as part of the statistical production cycle and includes analysis of methods and procedures affecting edited data. The subprocess requires subject-matter and methodological capability to judge whether data should be changed, assess impacts of edits/imputations on outputs, and recommend improved methods. This work description satisfies that need through the activity: 'participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.' It further requires 'knowledge of the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data' and research responsibility to 'analyze current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.' Those elements are highly relevant to modern statistical methods, methodological innovation, and adapting editing/imputation approaches to changing source environments.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected because it explicitly performs editing and validation of data and assesses data quality from systems and databases, which are core functions of subprocess 5.4. The subprocess requires capability to detect inconsistent or unreliable records, apply corrections, validate outputs, and work within production environments. This work description directly states 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data' and 'Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases.' It also includes research responsibilities to 'analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness' and to 'examine operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems.' These are strong matches to edit/impute needs and to drivers concerning integrated pipelines, automation, system changes, and operational efficiency. Its contextual knowledge explicitly references 'editing, validation' procedures and compliance requirements in handling statistical data.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because subprocess 5.4 explicitly includes 'producing metadata on the editing and imputation process,' including flags, documentation, lineage and standardized descriptions of changes made to data. The subprocess therefore needs capability to prepare, validate, store and evaluate metadata associated with edits and imputations in reproducible pipelines. This work description satisfies that need through responsibility to 'prepare, edit, validate and disseminate statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository.' It also provides 'assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies' and analyzes methods for 'producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata.' Its knowledge of 'statistical metadata concepts and frameworks,' 'methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata,' and awareness of collection, processing and dissemination contexts make it materially relevant to metadata, standards, discoverability and traceability drivers, though it is less directly responsible for performing the edits or imputations themselves.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role has only indirect relevance to subprocess 5.4. Edit and impute requires analytical handling of quantitative and qualitative data, assessment of data requirements, and interpretation of data quality issues, all of which this role touches in a general evaluation context. The work description includes 'identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data,' 'gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases,' and 'provides input on the interpretation of data.' These capabilities could support understanding data issues or evaluating methods, but the role does not explicitly mention statistical processing, editing, imputation, validation workflows, metadata flags, or automated production systems. Therefore it is only weakly connected compared with roles that directly perform data processing and editing.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is directly connected to deriving new variables and units because the subprocess centers on transforming existing data into new analytical variables, potentially using iterative logic, modelling and modern tools. The relevant aspect of the subprocess is the creation of derived variables through arithmetic formulae, transformation, modelling and use of integrated data assets. The capability needed is hands-on data transformation, modelling, data quality assessment, and use of statistical programming tools in a modern analytics environment. This work description satisfies that need through explicit responsibility for "data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin" and for supporting studies using "Python, SAS, STATA, R, E-Views, SPSS or other similar software." It also evidences capability aligned to AI/automation and methodological innovation through knowledge of the data science life cycle including "processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization" and "predictive analysis," as well as knowledge of statistics and mathematics "to conduct the requisite modelling." Its requirement to liaise with subject matter and systems specialists to translate requirements into specifications also aligns with orchestrated, reusable derivation pipelines and integrated processing.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially implicated because derived variables and units must be consistently defined, documented, validated and made reusable across programs, which is central to the metadata and standards driver for subprocess 5.5. The relevant aspect of the subprocess is documenting derivation logic, variable definitions, quality indicators and ensuring discoverability and reuse of derived outputs. The capability needed is statistical metadata production, validation, standards application, and assessment of impacts of changed methods and systems on metadata. This work description satisfies that need by explicitly "prepar[ing], edit[ing], validat[ing] and disseminat[ing] statistical metadata" and ensuring it is "correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository." It also provides evidence of responsibility for advising on "documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines," participating in testing "new procedures and systems," and analyzing changes in methods and systems "to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats." Knowledge requirements include "statistical metadata concepts and frameworks," methods for "producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata," and knowledge of survey and statistical program methodologies relevant to "collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data," all of which are directly relevant to derived-variable definitions and lineage.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is strongly connected to deriving new variables and units because the subprocess often requires subject-matter-informed transformations, estimation logic, and assessment of how concepts, definitions and processing choices affect outputs. The relevant aspect of the subprocess is deriving analytically meaningful variables and possibly units from collected and processed data, especially where model assumptions or alternative manipulations are involved. The capability needed is subject-matter analysis, statistical estimation and modelling knowledge, and the ability to assess impacts of concepts, definitions and processing methods on resulting data. This work description satisfies that need through knowledge of "statistical or economic theory and principles" and "methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling." It also explicitly requires assessing "the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data." The role further analyzes "current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems," which aligns with iterative derivation logic, methodological innovation, and integration of derivation into broader processing workflows.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because deriving new variables and units depends on operational processing environments, sequencing, system requirements and reliable data flows, especially under the integrated pipelines and orchestration driver. The relevant aspect of the subprocess is the implementation and maintenance of manual and automated processing operations that support derivation routines and ensure reliable execution order and data consistency. The capability needed is operational knowledge of processing systems, data flows, verification methods, and assessment of system requirements and source/output changes. This work description satisfies that need by participating in "manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data" and by having knowledge of "systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows" for "regular production of statistical data and for ad hoc manipulations and retrievals." It also "assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers" and "analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results." While the role is not explicitly focused on deriving variables itself, it materially supports the operational environment in which derivation logic is executed and controlled.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected because derived variables and units become part of validated statistical outputs, and this position assesses processed data, adapts data to new definitions, and evaluates effects of revised processing specifications. The relevant aspect of the subprocess is the downstream validation, adaptation and interpretation of derived data products, including ensuring that transformed variables remain coherent and usable. The capability needed is assessment of processed data validity, interpretation of alternative manipulations, and adaptation of data to revised definitions or formats. This work description satisfies that need through knowledge of "the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data." It also "compiles data from diverse sources," "analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness," and "adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats." In addition, it "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions," which links to orchestrated derivation pipelines and integrated processing. The role is less directly responsible for creating derivations than analyst or methodological roles, but it is still materially implicated.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role has only an indirect connection to subprocess 5.5. The relevant aspect is the use and interpretation of quantitative and qualitative data, including support for assessing data requirements and analyzing databases, which may involve working with already-derived variables in evaluation contexts. The capability needed would be general analytical ability to gather, analyze and synthesize data and to interpret findings. This work description satisfies that need only broadly: it "identify[ies], gather[s], analyz[es] and synthesiz[es] quantitative and qualitative data," "gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases," and "provides input on the interpretation of data." However, there is no explicit evidence of responsibility for deriving new statistical variables or units, implementing transformation logic, managing metadata for derivations, or designing processing pipelines. Therefore the connection is limited and low.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is materially connected to calculating weights because the subprocess requires quantitative statistical processing, data preparation, modelling, validation, and use of analytical software, all of which are central to this role. The subprocess relevance is the creation and application of record-level weights, including adjustment, normalization, and benchmarking in recurring production. The needed capability is statistical modelling, data transformation, quality assessment, and use of tools that support increasingly automated and reproducible weighting workflows under drivers such as AI and Automation, Integrated Data Pipelines, Administrative and Alternative Data, and Modern Statistical Methods. This role satisfies that need through key activities such as supporting studies using 'quantitative statistical data analysis methods and software such as Python, SAS, STATA, R', and conducting 'data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality'. Evidence also includes knowledge of 'theories, principles, practices, and methodologies of statistics and mathematics in order to conduct the requisite modelling', knowledge of 'survey methodologies, data risk assessment, impact and quantitative analysis', and knowledge of the data science life cycle including 'processing, mining, clustering, modeling'. These elements directly support implementation and operationalization of weighting methods.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is strongly implicated because weight calculation depends on statistical estimation methods, assessment of methodological impacts, and analysis of how collection and processing conditions affect outputs. The subprocess relevance is the methodological and analytical side of weighting, including calibration, nonresponse adjustment, and assessing representativeness and bias under changing data sources. The needed capability is knowledge of estimation, statistical methods, and the ability to analyze effects of methodological and processing changes on results. This work description satisfies that need through explicit knowledge of 'methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling' and through participation in analysis of data with feedback on 'collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures'. Evidence also includes research responsibilities to 'analyze changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output' and to 'assess and determine the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored.' Those responsibilities align closely with weighting work affected by methodological innovation and alternative data.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because calculate weights is a production subprocess that must operate reliably within statistical processing systems and recurring workflows. The subprocess relevance is the operational implementation of weighting as part of manual and automated processing, including system requirements, data flows, and quality control. The needed capability is operational knowledge of statistical processing, verification, and impacts of source or system changes on output integrity, especially under the driver of Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration. This work description satisfies that need through key activities such as participating 'in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data' and evaluating 'methods, procedures and results'. Evidence includes knowledge of 'methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications', knowledge of 'systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows', and research responsibilities that 'analyse changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results' and 'assess and review system requirements' for processing systems. While not explicitly methodological on weighting, it is materially connected to operationalizing and controlling the weighting step.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is relevant because weighting affects the validity, consistency, and interpretation of processed statistical outputs, and this position reviews data quality from systems and processed data. The subprocess relevance is downstream validation and assessment of weighted outputs and the effects of revised processing specifications or methodologies on data products. The needed capability is evaluating processed data quality, understanding quantitative methods, and assessing impacts of system and methodological changes. This work description satisfies that need through key activities to 'review and assess data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases' and to edit and validate data. Evidence includes knowledge of 'quantitative analytical techniques', knowledge of 'socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data', and research responsibilities to 'analyze and evaluate data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness', 'analyze changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output', and examine 'new or revised processing specifications' for their effect on processing functions. This makes the role materially connected to weighted data production, though less directly responsible for deriving weights themselves.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated at a supporting level because weighting methods, parameters, quality indicators, and processing changes need to be documented, validated, and made reproducible across production cycles. The subprocess relevance is metadata support for standardized, auditable weighting processes under the driver of Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and for documenting methodological changes driven by innovation and alternative data. The needed capability is production, validation, and quality evaluation of statistical metadata tied to processing and methodology. This work description satisfies that need through key activities to 'prepare, edit, validate and disseminate statistical metadata' and provide feedback on methods and procedures for producing and evaluating metadata. Evidence includes knowledge of 'survey and statistical program subject matter concepts and methodologies relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data', analysis of 'changes in methods, procedures and systems used to produce, store, disseminate and evaluate the quality of statistical metadata', and interpreting client requirements for metadata production and quality evaluation. The connection is indirect but material because weighting requires clear metadata and documentation for reproducibility and auditability.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is directly connected to calculating aggregates because the subprocess requires transforming microdata into totals, averages, dispersion measures and other summaries using statistical software and reproducible processing steps. The subprocess is also influenced by integrated pipelines, alternative data, cloud processing and modern methods, all of which require capability in data preparation, processing, quality assessment and statistical analysis. This work description satisfies that need through explicit responsibilities for 'data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin' and support for studies using 'quantitative statistical data analysis methods and software such as Python, SAS, STATA, R'. It also references knowledge of the data science lifecycle including 'processing', 'summarization', 'reporting', and knowledge of 'theories, principles, practices, and methodologies of statistics and mathematics'. These are materially aligned with producing aggregates from microdata and adapting aggregation workflows to automated and scalable environments.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is strongly implicated because calculating aggregates is a statistical compilation activity requiring understanding of estimation, data validity, compilation methods and the effects of methodological or processing changes on outputs. The subprocess specifically includes deriving totals from lower-level data and may include sampling error calculation; this requires analytical and methodological capability. This work description satisfies that need through participation in 'the analysis of statistical program data', feedback on 'collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures', and knowledge of 'statistical estimation'. It also explicitly requires 'Knowledge of statistical or economic theory and principles ... and the methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling' and 'Knowledge of the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data'. Its research component includes analyzing 'current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures' and assessing impacts of changes in methodology and technology on outputs. That is materially relevant to aggregate calculation and to drivers such as methodological innovation, integrated pipelines and alternative data.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is directly implicated because aggregate calculation often results in statistical tables and custom tabulations for users, and requires validation of outputs from systems and databases. The subprocess concerns creating aggregate data and totals from microdata or lower-level aggregates, and this role explicitly works with producing and interpreting such outputs. The needed capability is to compile data from multiple sources, create tabulations, assess output quality, and adapt outputs to changing methods and systems. This work description satisfies that need through key activities such as 'Interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations' and 'Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases.' The evidence is especially strong in research and analysis: 'Compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output. Summarizes and describes meaning of data. Analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness.' It also includes analyzing effects of changes in 'procedures, methodology, computer technology' on outputs, which aligns with drivers around pipelines, cloud infrastructure, open-source tooling and methodological innovation.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected because aggregate calculation depends on reliable processing operations, data flows, system requirements and quality controls in both manual and automated environments. While the role is broader and more upstream than direct statistical aggregation, the subprocess drivers emphasize governed downstream automation, reproducible execution and scalable processing, which require operational support. The needed capability is to maintain and improve processing systems, verify data reliability and understand impacts of source and output changes on production results. This work description satisfies that need through participation in 'manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data', knowledge of 'methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications', and contextual knowledge of 'computer processing and data flows' for 'regular production of statistical data and for ad hoc manipulations and retrievals.' Its research component includes analyzing 'changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results' and assessing system requirements for new processing systems. This is relevant to automated aggregate production pipelines, though less directly focused on the statistical calculation itself.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because aggregate calculation in modern pipelines depends on well-managed metadata, standards, documentation, lineage and quality evaluation, especially under drivers such as integrated pipelines, reusable architecture and cloud infrastructure. The subprocess itself creates aggregates, but reproducible and governed aggregation requires metadata about concepts, methods, classifications, processing and dissemination. The needed capability is to manage and evaluate metadata that supports consistent aggregate production and interpretation across programs. This work description satisfies that need through responsibilities to 'prepare, edit, validate and disseminate statistical metadata', provide advice on 'documented standards and relevant policies', and participate in testing 'new procedures and systems.' It also requires knowledge of 'survey and statistical program subject matter concepts and methodologies relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data' and analysis of 'current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems'. This is materially relevant to the governance and reproducibility aspects of aggregate calculation, though not to performing the calculations directly.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role has a limited but still material connection because it involves quantitative data analysis, synthesis and summarization, which overlap conceptually with aggregate production. However, the role is oriented toward program evaluation rather than statistical production, and it does not explicitly address compilation of official statistical aggregates, weighting, tabulation pipelines or uncertainty estimation. The relevant subprocess aspect is the need to analyze and synthesize quantitative data into findings and summaries. The needed capability is basic quantitative analysis and interpretation of data. This work description satisfies that need through tasks such as 'identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data' and applying 'analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of evaluation results'. It also mentions applying methods for 'sorting, summarizing, analyzing and interpreting data.' These elements are adjacent to aggregate calculation, but the connection is weaker than roles explicitly focused on statistical processing, compilation or tabulation.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is directly connected to finalising data files because the subprocess centers on assembling processed outputs into an analysis-ready dataset, and this position explicitly performs core preparation activities needed for that handoff. The subprocess requires capability in extracting, cleansing, transforming, validating and organizing data into usable files, often within automated or standardized pipelines influenced by AI, orchestration and cloud-based processing. This work description satisfies that need through duties such as 'conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin' and 'organizes and consolidates information relevant to the defined objectives of studies. Maintains work files.' It also aligns with driver-related needs for pipeline-based and governed production because it requires knowledge of 'data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing' and includes 'data stewardship' plus the ability to 'protect and secure data' and knowledge of policies for 'handling, tracking, filing and storing of sensitive and confidential material and information holdings, including electronic records.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: Finalising data files increasingly depends on complete, standardized metadata, repository loading, documentation and quality evaluation so that the resulting dataset can be reliably handed to analysis and reused later. This is especially material under the drivers for metadata standards, integrated pipelines, multi-source data and discoverability. The subprocess needs capability to package final datasets with metadata, validate metadata quality, and ensure storage and dissemination structures are consistent and governed. This work description directly satisfies that need because it 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository' and 'participates on teams tasked with the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.' Evidence also includes knowledge of 'methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata,' ability to analyze changes in systems 'to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats,' and awareness of 'security and confidentiality of statistical information' for compliance.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is strongly implicated because finalising data files is fundamentally about editing, validating, integrating and preparing data outputs for downstream use, and this position explicitly works on those functions. The subprocess requires responsibility for validating processed data, assessing output quality from systems and databases, adapting outputs to required formats, and supporting dissemination-ready packaging. This work description satisfies that need through key activities such as 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data' and 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases.' Its research and analysis responsibilities are especially aligned with final file assembly: it 'compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output,' 'analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness,' 'examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems,' and 'adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats, depending on the complexity of the subject matter or the number of different sources.' These directly support integrated pipelines, multi-source assembly, versioned outputs and analysis-ready packaging.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: The subprocess is materially connected to this role because finalising data files depends on the operational processing environment that assembles, verifies and controls processed data outputs. The drivers emphasize automation, orchestration, cloud repositories, security and standardized production, all of which require operational capability in manual and automated processing, data flow understanding, system requirements and output integrity. This work description satisfies that need because it 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data' and has knowledge of 'systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows' for 'the maintenance and use of databases both for regular production of statistical data and for ad hoc manipulations and retrievals.' It also includes 'knowledge of methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications,' 'assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers,' and 'analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results.' Security relevance is explicit through awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts 'with respect to the security and confidentiality of data.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because finalising data files requires subject-matter assessment of whether processed and compiled data are valid, coherent and suitable for analysis, especially when outputs are affected by changing methods, definitions, processing conditions or integrated sources. The subprocess needs capability to assess the impact of processing and storage conditions on final analytical datasets and to propose improvements to processing and compilation methods. This work description satisfies that need through activities that include participating in analysis of data and suggesting feedback on 'collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures.' Supporting evidence includes knowledge 'to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data,' and research responsibilities that 'assess and determine the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored' and 'analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.' This is relevant to final file readiness, though the role is more evaluative and subject-matter oriented than directly responsible for file assembly.
