implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is directly connected to subprocess 6.1 because the subprocess is about transforming finalized data into draft statistical outputs and accompanying explanatory material. The role's core responsibilities align with producing and disseminating outputs: it 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data,' 'interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations,' and 'provides statistical data and consultative services to users.' The subprocess specifically includes outputs such as tables, analytical products and explanatory notes; this role explicitly 'compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output,' 'summarizes and describes meaning of data,' and 'drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data and the concepts, methods and techniques used.' These responsibilities satisfy the need to prepare draft outputs and methodological explanations. It is also materially connected to the drivers: changes in methods, technology and processing are part of the role, as shown by 'analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services,' which supports AI/automation, modern methods, reusable tools and integrated pipelines. The role also 'adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats,' which is relevant to standardized metadata-driven and reusable output production.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is strongly implicated because subprocess 6.1 requires analysis of processed data and preparation of draft analytical outputs for publication. The work description states that the position 'participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes' and 'identifies statistical trends and developments.' That is a direct match to preparing draft outputs from finalized data. The subprocess also requires explanation of methods and presentation choices; this role contributes by 'participat[ing] in the analysis of data and suggest[ing] possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures' and by writing 'detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional systems and applications.' This satisfies the need for analytical interpretation and clear communication of outputs and methods. The role is also relevant to drivers concerning methodological innovation and changing production environments because it 'analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services' and 'assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored.' That evidence connects it to explaining newer methods, alternative data conditions, and implications for users.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is highly relevant because subprocess 6.1 explicitly includes preparation of methodological notes and explanatory metadata to make outputs understandable, searchable and reusable. The role's central function is to 'prepare, edit, validate and disseminate statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository.' It also 'provides assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines' and 'provides input to documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals related to the production and dissemination of statistical metadata.' These responsibilities directly satisfy the need for structural and explanatory metadata accompanying draft outputs. The drivers make metadata and discoverability especially important, and this role contains explicit evidence of capability in that area: 'knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks,' 'knowledge of methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata,' and 'contributes written information... to reports which describe the results of metadata quality evaluations.' It is also relevant to integrated pipelines and reusable architecture because the role analyzes 'changes in methods, procedures and systems used to produce, store, disseminate and evaluate the quality of statistical metadata' and determines where updates are required to documentation and manuals.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected because subprocess 6.1 increasingly depends on analytical tooling, visualization, modern methods and clear communication of results, especially under AI/automation and open-source tool drivers. The role 'supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods and software such as Python, SAS, STATA, R, E-Views, SPSS or other similar software,' which is relevant to generating draft outputs from finalized data. It also includes knowledge of the full analytics lifecycle, including 'summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence' and the ability to 'read, analyze, interpret, visualize and communicate data.' This satisfies the need for producing analytical outputs, charts and explanatory materials. The communication evidence is also relevant: 'writing skills are necessary to draft clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools for managers and clients with varying levels of knowledge and understanding of data science.' The role is less directly tied than dissemination/output-specific roles because its key activities focus more on data preparation and analytical support than on formal publication outputs or methodological notes, but it remains materially implicated due to modern tool use, visualization, reporting and advanced analytics capabilities.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is relevant because subprocess 6.1 depends on operationalized production of outputs and explanatory materials, especially where integrated pipelines, automation and standardized production services affect how outputs are generated. Although the role is rooted in collection/coding/processing operations, it includes direct output-preparation tasks: it 'designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications.' That is a direct connection to preparing draft outputs. It also 'writes survey information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports,' which supports the subprocess need for supporting documentation and explanatory material. The role's contextual and analytical responsibilities connect to the drivers: it has 'knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows' for 'regular production of statistical data and for ad hoc manipulations and retrievals,' and it 'analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results.' This satisfies needs arising from integrated pipelines, cloud/shared services, and reusable production processes. Relevance is medium rather than high because the role's primary focus is upstream operations rather than analytical drafting and methodological explanation.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role has a limited but material connection to subprocess 6.1 through its responsibilities for analyzing data and contributing to reports and presentations. The subprocess requires transforming data into outputs and explanatory material; this role 'identif[ies], gather[s], analyz[es] and synthesiz[es] quantitative and qualitative data' and 'provides the Evaluation Manager with supporting data for sections of reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda.' It also 'provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions.' These capabilities partially satisfy the need for analytical interpretation and drafting supporting narrative. However, the role is oriented to program evaluation studies rather than statistical production outputs, and there is no direct evidence of responsibility for statistical dissemination products, metadata, tabulations, charts for publication, or methodological notes tied to statistical outputs. Therefore it is implicated only at a low level.

Relevant aspects of the subprocess include validating outputs, comparing related outputs, assessing effects of methodological or system changes, and adapting outputs from multiple sources. The capability needed is responsibility for editing and validating data, assessing output quality, interpreting changes in methods and systems, and comparing outputs across sources. This work description satisfies that need through key activities such as 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data' and 'Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases.' It also provides direct evidence of output validation responsibilities in research and analysis: 'Compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output... Analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness,' 'Analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services,' and 'Knowledge of data sources within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare related statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability.' This aligns strongly with drivers on AI/automation, alternative data, modern methods, metadata-driven quality checks, and efficiency-oriented validation.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected because Validate outputs requires subject-matter analysis, checking divergence from expectations, assessing validity of outputs, and understanding how collection, processing, editing and compilation affect results. The capability needed is analytical and domain expertise to judge whether outputs are credible, coherent and consistent with concepts, methods and prior knowledge. This work description satisfies that need through key activities such as 'participates in the analysis of statistical program data,' 'Identifies statistical trends and developments,' and 'participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures.' Evidence is especially strong in the knowledge and analysis sections: 'Knowledge of the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data,' 'Knowledge of data sources within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare related statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability,' 'Assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored,' and 'Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.' This is highly relevant to validation under changing methods, linked or alternative data, and model-based outputs.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is directly implicated because the subprocess includes data validation, anomaly detection, quality assessment, and use of analytical tools to validate outputs under increasingly automated and methodologically advanced production. The capability needed is practical data analysis and validation skill, including use of statistical software, data quality assessment, and understanding of the data lifecycle. This work description satisfies that need through key activities such as 'Supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods and software such as Python, SAS, STATA, R,' and 'Conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin.' Supporting evidence includes knowledge of 'data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization, reporting, visualization,' as well as 'Knowledge of techniques and methods of information collection and analysis... in order to assess the quality of data and identify and mitigate risks to its integrity' and 'Data literacy includes data stewardship and the ability to assess the quality of data.' This aligns strongly with AI and automation, integrated pipelines, modern methods, and workforce skills transition affecting output validation.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is highly relevant because the subprocess explicitly includes checking that metadata, paradata and quality indicators are present and in line with expectations. The capability needed is preparation, validation and quality evaluation of statistical metadata within a standards-driven environment, plus liaison with subject matter and survey staff to ensure metadata completeness and consistency. This work description satisfies that need through key activities such as 'Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata,' 'assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations,' and 'participates on teams tasked with the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.' Evidence directly matching the subprocess includes knowledge of 'statistical metadata concepts and frameworks' used 'to prepare, edit and validate statistical metadata,' knowledge of 'methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata,' and research/analysis responsibilities such as 'Evaluates selected indicators of statistical metadata quality across survey and statistical programs in accordance with pre-defined quality guidelines' and 'Compiles information from diverse sources in order to prepare, edit, validate and evaluate statistical metadata.' This is especially implicated by the metadata and standards driver and by integrated pipelines requiring systematic metadata and quality checkpoints.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected because Validate outputs depends on understanding how collection, coding and processing operations affect output quality, consistency and reliability, especially when source changes or pipeline changes occur. The capability needed is operational knowledge of verification methods, data flows, source changes, and the ability to analyze impacts on program results. This work description satisfies that need through key activities such as participating in 'manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data' and 'Evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives.' Evidence includes 'Knowledge of methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications,' 'Knowledge of data sources and contacts within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability,' 'Analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results,' and communication requirements to resolve issues affecting 'the efficiency of the division's operations and quality of outputs.' This is relevant particularly for integrated pipelines, alternative data, and efficiency-driven validation, though the role is more upstream operational than directly centered on final output validation.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role has some connection because the subprocess includes gathering intelligence, analyzing quantitative and qualitative data, and forming evidence-based conclusions, all of which resemble evaluation-oriented analytical work. The capability needed is general research, data synthesis and interpretation to support judgments about findings. This work description satisfies that need in part through activities such as 'identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data,' 'applying analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of evaluation results and formulating conclusions,' and 'Provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions.' Supporting evidence also includes knowledge of statistics and research methods and the ability to collect data from diverse sources. However, the role is focused on program evaluation studies rather than statistical production output validation, and it does not explicitly address validating statistical outputs, comparing time series, checking metadata/quality indicators, or assessing production-system effects. Therefore it is only low relevance.

Subprocess 6.3 requires interpreting outputs from multiple perspectives, using different tools and media, and explaining results produced through modernized methods; this role provides that capability through knowledge of data science lifecycle activities including mining, clustering, modeling, summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence, and exploratory/confirmatory and predictive analysis. It also addresses the drivers: AI and Automation and Modern Statistical Methods are reflected in its knowledge of modeling and advanced analytics; Administrative and Alternative Data is reflected in assessing data quality, conformity to standards, and data origin; Workforce Transformation is reflected in the need for advanced interpretation, visualization and communication skills; and Open-Source Enablement is reflected in use of tools such as Python and R. Evidence includes: 'Supports the conduct of studies... using... Python, SAS, STATA, R'; 'Conducts data preparation... ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin'; 'Writing skills are necessary to draft clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools... Information must be impartial and clearly presented to minimize the potential for misinterpretation'; and 'Data literacy includes... read, analyze, interpret, visualize and communicate data'.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially implicated because it explicitly participates in the analysis of statistical program data, identifies statistical trends and developments, and assesses how concepts, definitions, collection conditions, processing and methodology affect results. That is central to subprocess 6.3, which requires understanding the meaning of outputs and explaining them in light of how they were produced. The role is especially relevant to drivers concerning administrative/alternative data and methodological innovation because it assesses 'the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored' and analyzes changes in procedures and methodology to determine effects on outputs. It also supports explanation of model- or method-driven outputs through knowledge of statistical estimation and economic modeling, and communication of technical concepts in common terminology. Evidence includes: 'participates in the analysis of statistical program data'; 'Identifies statistical trends and developments'; 'Knowledge of statistical or economic theory... and the methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling'; 'Analyzes changes in procedures, methodology... to determine the effect on data output'; and 'Assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is strongly connected to interpreting and explaining outputs because it not only disseminates data but also summarizes and describes the meaning of data, analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness, and drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data. Subprocess 6.3 requires explaining outputs, assessing them against expectations, and understanding methodological effects; this role directly supports those needs through quality review, interpretation for users, and analysis of how procedural or methodological changes affect outputs. It is also relevant to drivers on administrative/alternative data and modern methods because it reviews data quality from new and modified systems and databases, adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats, and analyzes changes in procedures and methodology. Evidence includes: 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data'; 'Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases'; 'Drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data and the concepts, methods and techniques used'; 'Compiles data from diverse sources... Summarizes and describes meaning of data. Analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness'; and 'Analyzes changes in procedures, methodology... to determine the effect on data output, products and services.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is relevant because it includes analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data, applying analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of results, formulating conclusions, and providing input on interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions. These responsibilities align with subprocess 6.3's need to interpret outputs and explain their meaning. It also supports the workforce transformation and modern methods drivers through participation in socio-economic and cost-benefit analyses and recommending enhancements to methods for retrieving data and information. However, the role is framed around program evaluation rather than core statistical output interpretation, so the connection is material but less direct than analyst or subject-matter roles. Evidence includes: 'identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data'; 'applying analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of evaluation results and formulating conclusions'; 'Provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions'; and 'participates in the conduct of socio-economic analyses and cost-benefit analysis'.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because subprocess 6.3 requires interpreting outputs based on an understanding of how results were produced, and metadata is essential for explaining concepts, methods, source changes, quality and comparability. The role supports that need by preparing, validating and evaluating statistical metadata; understanding survey and statistical program methodologies; and contributing to metadata quality reports. It is particularly relevant to drivers involving administrative and alternative data and methodological innovation, since interpretation must account for source effects, linkage artifacts, coverage differences and methodological changes, all of which depend on accurate metadata. It is less directly involved in substantive analysis of outputs, so relevance is medium rather than high. Evidence includes: 'Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata'; 'assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations and provides input to reports'; 'Knowledge of survey and statistical program subject matter concepts and methodologies relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data'; and 'Analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems... to determine the need to update statistical metadata'.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is relevant because interpreting outputs in subprocess 6.3 depends on understanding collection, coding and processing effects on results. The role analyzes changes to data sources and outputs, determines impacts on integrity and completeness of program results, and reports on problems encountered in implementing concepts, definitions and classifications. This supports explanation of outputs where source changes, operational issues or processing differences may affect interpretation, especially under the administrative/alternative data and methodological innovation drivers. It also contributes explanatory text and statistical tables/charts, which supports communication of outputs. The role is not primarily responsible for substantive analytical interpretation, so relevance is medium. Evidence includes: 'Evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results'; 'Designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text'; 'Analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results'; and 'Analyses reported data and work results... recommending alternatives.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is directly implicated because subprocess 6.4 applies confidentiality rules to data before dissemination, including output checking and protection of released tables or custom outputs. The subprocess is especially relevant to this position's responsibilities for disseminating data and creating custom statistical tabulations, where disclosure risk must be assessed before release. The needed capability is to evaluate outputs, apply organizational policies and legal requirements, and ensure confidentiality in dissemination. This work description satisfies that need through key activities such as 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data' and 'Interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations.' It also explicitly requires 'particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data' and knowledge of policies for 'editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data.' Its research responsibilities include compiling data into 'charts, tables and other output' and interpreting user requests for feasible information provision, which is materially connected to disclosure control for aggregate and potentially sensitive outputs. The drivers strengthen relevance: linked administrative/alternative data increase re-identification risk in disseminated outputs; privacy and secure access are explicitly central; and digital platforms affect dissemination channels.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected because subprocess 6.4 explicitly covers both data and metadata to be disseminated or internally stored, ensuring they do not breach confidentiality rules. The relevant aspect is protection and quality control of statistical metadata during production, storage and dissemination, including compliance with confidentiality and privacy requirements. The needed capability is to manage metadata under policy controls, understand dissemination procedures, and ensure metadata handling does not expose confidential statistical information. This work description satisfies that need through key activities such as 'Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata' and participation in teams for the 'production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.' Evidence is especially strong in contextual knowledge: 'The position must have an awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information to ensure that actions are in compliance,' and 'Knowledge of the Statistics Act and of Statistics Canada policies, directives and guidelines' for metadata production and dissemination. The role also analyzes methods and systems for producing, storing and disseminating metadata, which aligns with cloud/platform and secure-access drivers affecting controlled storage and dissemination environments.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because disclosure control depends on assessing data quality, risk, governance and responsible use before outputs are released or reused, particularly under AI/automation and linked administrative data drivers. The relevant subprocess aspect is preparation and analysis of data in ways that preserve confidentiality and support secure, policy-compliant use of sensitive data assets. The needed capability is data risk assessment, protection of sensitive/confidential material, and advising on governance concepts that protect data utility while safeguarding privacy. This work description satisfies that need through responsibilities to conduct 'data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin' and to provide 'advice, information and guidance to data users and clients regarding governance concepts used to protect and optimize the utility of Statistics Canada's data assets.' Evidence also includes knowledge of 'data risk assessment,' 'data stewardship,' the ability to 'protect and secure data, and safeguard their responsible use,' and 'basic knowledge of ... policies pertaining to the handling, tracking, filing and storing of sensitive and confidential material.' While the role does not explicitly state disclosure control or dissemination approval, its governance, risk and secure-data responsibilities materially support subprocess 6.4.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is connected because subprocess 6.4 occurs within analysis and requires analysts working with statistical outputs to understand confidentiality constraints when preparing material for internal use and publication. The relevant aspect is assessing how methods, outputs and presentation approaches may affect what can be safely released. The needed capability is analytical judgment about outputs, awareness of legal and policy confidentiality requirements, and ability to adjust methods or presentation accordingly. This work description satisfies that need through key activities including participation 'in the analysis of statistical program data' and assisting 'in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.' It also includes analysis of 'collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures' and assessing impacts of concepts and conditions under which data was 'processed and stored.' Crucially, contextual knowledge requires 'particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data.' This makes the role materially relevant, though less directly than dissemination-focused roles because disclosure control is not named as a primary responsibility.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because disclosure control is influenced by how data are processed, verified, stored and operationalized, especially under digital platforms/cloud and privacy/security drivers. The relevant subprocess aspect is ensuring operational systems and data flows support confidentiality protection before outputs are released or stored for future use. The needed capability is operational control over processing methods, awareness of confidentiality obligations, and understanding of system/data-flow implications for secure handling. This work description satisfies that need through participation in 'manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' evaluation of methods and procedures, and preparation of outputs such as 'statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text.' Evidence includes contextual knowledge of 'systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows' and explicit awareness of 'the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data.' The role also analyzes changes to 'data sources and outputs' for impacts on integrity and completeness, which is relevant where linked administrative or alternative data increase disclosure risk. Relevance is medium because the role supports confidentiality-aware operations but is not explicitly responsible for disclosure control decisions.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role has a limited but material connection because subprocess 6.4 concerns handling and analysis of potentially sensitive data and metadata under confidentiality rules, and this position gathers, analyzes and synthesizes quantitative and qualitative data for evaluation studies. The relevant aspect is responsible handling and interpretation of data used in studies, potentially including sensitive administrative or program information. The needed capability is careful data use, analysis and communication with awareness of organizational policies. This work description satisfies that need indirectly through activities such as 'identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data' and 'gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases.' It also requires knowledge of Statistics Canada 'accountabilities and policies.' However, there is no explicit evidence of confidentiality, privacy, disclosure control, dissemination approval, or secure access responsibilities in the description. Therefore the connection is low and mainly contextual rather than direct.

However, the role is oriented to program evaluation studies rather than statistical output finalization, and it does not explicitly cover dissemination metadata, release caveats, approval workflows, or publication readiness. Therefore relevance is low.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is directly implicated because subprocess 7.1 centers on formatting, loading, validating and linking metadata in dissemination-ready output systems. The subprocess specifically requires that metadata be formatted and loaded into output systems and that data be linked to relevant metadata, with a final check that all necessary metadata are in place. This position explicitly 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository,' which is a direct match to updating dissemination output systems. The subprocess also requires capability in metadata standards, storage, dissemination procedures, and quality checks; this role provides that through knowledge of 'statistical metadata concepts and frameworks,' 'methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata,' and analysis to 'determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats.' It also supports the strategic drivers around automation, integrated pipelines, cloud/shared repositories, metadata standards, discoverability, and secure dissemination because the work includes participating in testing 'new procedures and systems,' analyzing changes in methods and systems, and maintaining compliance with policies and confidentiality requirements, including awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected because subprocess 7.1 concerns the final preparation and loading of dissemination-ready data into output systems, including validation and adaptation to required formats. The position's core activities include 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data' and 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases,' which aligns closely with updating dissemination databases and output platforms. The subprocess needs capability to ensure data are correctly formatted, loaded, quality-checked, and usable in dissemination systems; this role satisfies that need through responsibilities to compile data into 'statistical charts, tables and other output,' analyze and evaluate data 'for consistency, reliability and appropriateness,' and 'adapt data to new definitions or presentation formats.' It is also relevant to drivers concerning integrated pipelines, digital platforms, automation, and operational efficiency because the role 'examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems.' Security and controlled dissemination are also supported by its required knowledge of the Statistics Act, policies, and 'particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because subprocess 7.1 depends on operational data flows, database maintenance, system specifications, and reliable movement of data into dissemination-ready environments. Although the role is broader and focused earlier in the production chain, it includes participation in 'manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data' and knowledge of 'systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows' for 'the application and conversion of databases, and the maintenance and use of databases both for regular production of statistical data and for ad hoc manipulations and retrievals.' The subprocess requires capability to support controlled loading and updating of output systems, especially under drivers related to automation, orchestration, cloud platforms, and efficiency. This role contributes by assessing 'system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems' and analyzing 'changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results.' It is also relevant to secure dissemination environments because it requires awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts and compliance in handling confidential data.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected through the subprocess need for data preparation, transformation, validation, standards conformance, and support to automated dissemination pipelines. Subprocess 7.1 requires formatting data and metadata for output systems and ensuring dissemination-ready content is correctly loaded and linked. This position performs 'data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin,' which are foundational capabilities for preparing outputs before loading into dissemination systems. It is especially relevant to drivers such as AI and Automation, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Open-Source enablement, and Operational Efficiency because the role uses analytical software and has knowledge of the data science lifecycle including 'data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing... summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence.' It also includes advising users on governance concepts and requires data stewardship skills, including the ability to 'protect and secure data,' which supports secure and controlled updating of dissemination outputs. However, it is less directly tied than dissemination-specific roles because it does not explicitly mention dissemination repositories or metadata linkage.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role has a secondary connection because subprocess 7.1 includes final preparation of outputs for dissemination and assessment of how procedural or system changes affect data products and services. The position participates in analysis for 'publication purposes' and has responsibilities related to 'collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical data,' which overlaps with dissemination readiness. The subprocess needs capability to understand how changes in methods, systems, and definitions affect output products; this role provides that through analysis of 'changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services' and through liaison to translate subject-matter requirements into 'specifications for system development.' It also has relevant contextual knowledge of policies and confidentiality obligations for presentation of data. However, the role is not directly focused on loading data/metadata into output systems or maintaining dissemination repositories, so the connection is limited.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is directly aligned to subprocess 7.2 because the subprocess is about producing dissemination products such as tables, downloadable files and publication-ready outputs, and this position explicitly performs dissemination work. The relevant subprocess aspects include assembling and adapting outputs for users, preparing statistical products, responding to user needs, and ensuring dissemination complies with policy and confidentiality requirements. The capability needed is the ability to edit, validate, format, interpret, and disseminate statistical data products, including custom tabulations and adaptation to new presentation formats in increasingly automated and standardized dissemination environments. This position satisfies that need through key activities such as: "Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data" and "Interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations." It also supports product creation through evidence that it "Compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output," "Adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats," and "Drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data... included in publications." The drivers are materially connected because the role addresses dissemination outputs, changing formats, effects of technology on products and services, and confidentiality: "Analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services" and has "particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data."

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is strongly implicated because subprocess 7.2 explicitly includes preparing explanatory texts, quality statements and dissemination-ready components, and several drivers emphasize metadata, standards, discoverability, interoperability and secure dissemination. The relevant subprocess aspect is the production of dissemination products that clearly expose metadata and quality information and are loaded into dissemination systems in standard formats. The capability needed is expertise in preparing, validating, storing and disseminating statistical metadata, advising clients on standards, and updating metadata methods and systems as dissemination processes become more automated and platform-based. This position satisfies that need through key activities such as: "Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository" and "Provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata; and participates in the testing of new procedures and systems." Evidence also shows direct support for standards and discoverability through knowledge of "statistical metadata concepts and frameworks... used... internationally" and "methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata." It is also relevant to confidentiality and controlled dissemination because the position requires awareness of "the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information." This directly supports drivers on metadata, digital platforms, orchestration, and secure publication.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is materially connected because subprocess 7.2 includes assembling product components, editing products and checking publication standards, and the drivers emphasize automation, templating, orchestrated workflows and efficient production. The relevant subprocess aspect is operational production of statistical outputs and preparation of publication components such as tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text. The capability needed is operational knowledge of manual and automated processes, production systems, data flows, and preparation of standard statistical output for publication. This position satisfies that need through evidence that it "Participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data" and "Designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications." It also supports workflow and system integration needs through knowledge of "systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows" and by "Assess[ing] and review[ing] system requirements" and analyzing changes to outputs. The role is less directly centered on dissemination than the dedicated dissemination positions, but it is still implicated because it contributes core product components and understands confidentiality obligations under the Statistics and Privacy Acts.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is relevant because subprocess 7.2 includes preparing analytical and explanatory material for publication and ensuring products are suitable for presentation to users. The relevant subprocess aspect is the preparation of analytical content and support to publication-oriented outputs, especially explanatory material accompanying statistical releases. The capability needed is subject-matter analysis, interpretation of trends, and the ability to translate technical concepts into publication-ready material while considering presentation methods and confidentiality. This position satisfies that need through the key activity: "Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes." Additional evidence includes that it "Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology" and analyzes "the effect on data output, products and services" as procedures and technology change. It also has contextual knowledge of "collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical data" and awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts. This makes it materially connected to dissemination product production, though less directly than roles explicitly responsible for dissemination operations.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is implicated at a lower level because several drivers for subprocess 7.2 emphasize automation, dashboards, visualization, data quality, standards and secure handling of data assets, all of which can support dissemination product production. The relevant subprocess aspect is preparation of clean, validated, standards-conformant data and creation of analytical reports, presentations and dashboards that may feed dissemination products. The capability needed is data preparation, validation, visualization and communication of data in forms suitable for downstream publication workflows. This position satisfies that need through key activities such as "Conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin." Evidence also includes knowledge of the data science life cycle including "summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence" and that "Writing skills are necessary to draft clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools" and to develop "briefings, presentations and dashboards that contain valid and reliable data." However, the role is not explicitly responsible for dissemination product assembly or publication, so relevance is lower.

drivers: Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration
Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is directly implicated because the subprocess is specifically about releasing dissemination products, including timing, subscriber provision, controlled access, communication of products, and possible correction or retraction. The relevant subprocess aspect is the operational release of statistical products to users. The needed capability is responsibility for disseminating data, responding to user requests, preparing outputs in usable formats, and applying policy and confidentiality requirements during release. This position satisfies that need because its core activities explicitly include to "edit, validate, market and disseminate data," "provide statistical data and consultative services to users," and "participate on data production and dissemination teams." It also supports release adaptation and downstream delivery through evidence that it "interprets user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required" and "adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats." The drivers strengthen relevance: digital platforms and automation affect dissemination workflows; cyber/privacy requirements align with its required awareness of "the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data"; and governance/timing pressures align with its role in operational dissemination and coordination.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is materially connected because release of dissemination products increasingly depends on metadata publication, discoverability, repository loading, standards compliance, and controlled access descriptions. The relevant subprocess aspect is ensuring all release elements are in place, especially metadata needed for publication, catalogue visibility, user understanding, and access conditions. The needed capability is production, validation, dissemination, and quality evaluation of statistical metadata, plus advice on policies, procedures, and systems supporting release. This position satisfies that need because it explicitly "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository" and "provides assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines." It also supports transformation drivers through evidence that it "provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata; and participates in the testing of new procedures and systems." This directly aligns with metadata/discoverability, digital platform release mechanisms, and process changes from automation/orchestration. Security and controlled access are also relevant because the description requires awareness of the "Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information."

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is implicated because release dissemination products often require analytical material for publication, explanation of concepts and methods, and support to users when products are released, especially where new data sources or methodological changes require careful communication and briefing. The relevant subprocess aspect is the preparation and communication of publication-ready analytical content and support to users around released products. The needed capability is analysis of statistical program data, preparation of material for publication, and explanation of technical concepts in accessible terms while respecting confidentiality and policy requirements. This position satisfies that need because it "participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes" and "provides data and assistance to users, within and outside Statistics Canada." It also includes communication evidence: "Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional systems and applications." Its contextual knowledge includes adherence to practices involved in the "presentation of statistical data" and awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts. Relevance is medium rather than high because the role supports publication content and user communication, but does not explicitly own release operations, embargoes, subscriber delivery, or access control.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is materially connected through the drivers rather than direct release ownership. The relevant subprocess aspect is readiness of dissemination products for release, especially data validation, quality assurance, governance of data use, and preparation of briefings, presentations, and dashboards that may accompany release. The needed capability is data preparation, validation, quality assessment, secure handling, and communication of analytical outputs to users and managers. This position satisfies that need because it "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin" and has writing responsibilities to "draft clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools for managers and clients." It also provides "advice, information and guidance to data users and clients regarding governance concepts used to protect and optimize the utility of Statistics Canada’s data assets" and requires "data stewardship" including the ability to "protect and secure data." These elements align with drivers on AI/automation, digital platforms, governance discipline, and cyber/privacy for controlled release environments. Relevance is medium because the role supports release quality and communication but does not explicitly perform dissemination operations.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description has a secondary connection because release dissemination depends on operational processes, system readiness, documentation, and secure handling of data, even though the role is centered earlier in the production chain. The relevant subprocess aspect is operational support for release readiness, including system/process coordination, explanatory materials, and handling of outputs used in publications. The needed capability is understanding operational systems, preparing reports and publication materials, and ensuring compliance with confidentiality requirements. This position satisfies that need through evidence that it "responds orally and in writing to enquiries ... to provide information on the operation of divisional systems and processes and the use of program results," "writes survey information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports," and "designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications." It also has contextual knowledge of "computer processing and data flows" and awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts. Relevance is low because the primary focus is collection, coding and processing operations rather than the actual release, timing control, subscriber distribution, embargo management, or access management described in subprocess 7.3.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is directly implicated because the subprocess is about actively promoting dissemination products, and this position explicitly includes both marketing and dissemination functions. The subprocess requires capability to market products, respond to user needs, and communicate statistical information in usable forms. This position satisfies that need through key activities such as "Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data," "Interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations," and "Provides statistical data and consultative services to users." It also supports promotion through communication products, as evidenced by "Drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data" and liaison with users and specialists. The discoverability-related driver is also relevant because the role adapts data to presentation formats and interprets user requests to determine feasible information products, evidenced by "Interprets user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required" and "Adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats."

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is materially connected because the subprocess explicitly mentions discoverability, product description, targeting users, and dissemination through searchable channels, all of which depend on strong metadata. The role requires capability to prepare, validate, disseminate and evaluate metadata that makes statistical products easier to find and understand. It satisfies that need through key activities such as "Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository" and "Provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata." The driver on metadata, standards and discoverability is especially relevant, supported by evidence including "Knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks... relating to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata," "Interprets client requirements in order to determine options for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata," and liaison work to "develop and translate requirements into specifications." This role also aligns with promotion support because well-structured metadata improves how products are surfaced and understood across dissemination channels.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is implicated because promoting dissemination products requires analytical content, interpretation, and presentation that help users understand and value the products being promoted. The role contributes to publication-oriented outputs and supports improvements to presentation methods. It satisfies this need through key activities such as "participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes," "Provides data and assistance to users," and participation in feedback on "presentation methods and procedures." Evidence also includes communication responsibilities to "write and present detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology" and research responsibilities to analyze "the effect on data output, products and services" and "current... presentation methods and procedures." This is relevant to promotion, but less directly than roles explicitly responsible for marketing, dissemination, or metadata.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is implicated mainly through support for data visualization, reporting, and user-oriented analytical products that can underpin dissemination promotion, as well as through the low-impact AI and automation driver. The subprocess requires capability to communicate statistical information effectively and potentially use automated or data-driven approaches to target or present products. This role satisfies part of that need through writing and visualization responsibilities, evidenced by "Writing skills are necessary to draft clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools" and communication with users and specialists to translate requirements. The AI and automation driver is relevant because the role requires knowledge of the data science life cycle, including "reporting, visualization, business intelligence" and advanced analytics methods. However, the role does not explicitly include dissemination promotion, marketing, CRM, websites, or metadata dissemination, so the connection is supportive rather than central.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description has a limited but material connection because promotion of dissemination products can depend on preparing publication-ready outputs and communicating program results, even though the role is primarily focused on collection and processing operations. It satisfies a supporting need through evidence such as "Responds orally and in writing to enquiries... to provide information on... the use of program results" and "Designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications." These activities can contribute to dissemination products that are later promoted. However, the role does not explicitly cover marketing, dissemination strategy, metadata discoverability, CRM, websites, or social media, so relevance is low.

Modular Reusable Architecture and Self-Service Tools

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is directly aligned with subprocess 7.5 because the subprocess centers on recording and responding to user queries, handling requests for services, and supporting dissemination users. The relevant aspect is front-line support for external and internal users seeking statistical outputs or custom services. The subprocess needs capability to interpret user requests, provide consultative services, explain data products, and respond within operational and policy constraints. This position satisfies that need because it explicitly 'Interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations' and 'Provides statistical data and consultative services to users.' It also supports dissemination operations through the key activity 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.' Evidence of user-support capability is further shown in research and analysis responsibilities: 'Interprets user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required,' and in communication duties such as drafting 'reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data and the concepts, methods and techniques used.' The role is also materially connected to drivers around privacy and secure access, metadata/discoverability, and efficiency because it requires 'particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data' and works within dissemination processes that can be standardized and supported by knowledge assets.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is strongly implicated because subprocess 7.5 includes helping users understand products, reducing repeated enquiries through knowledge bases/FAQ content, and supporting dissemination through better discoverability and explanation. The relevant aspect is support grounded in metadata, standards, documentation, and advice to clients. The subprocess needs capability to explain metadata, assist users with standards and policies, contribute to reusable documentation, and improve discoverability so users can self-serve where possible. This position satisfies that need because it 'provides assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines.' It also 'Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata' and 'Provides input to documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals related to the production and dissemination of statistical metadata and assists with the delivery of training.' These duties directly support the driver 'Metadata, Data Standards and Discoverability' and also support AI/automation and self-service models by creating structured metadata and documentation that can populate knowledge repositories. Evidence also includes communication responsibilities to 'develop and translate requirements into specifications' and to contribute written information for manuals and reports, plus contextual knowledge of 'policies, directives and guidelines directly and specifically related to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata' and awareness of 'the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information.'

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected because subprocess 7.5 includes recording and responding to user queries and requests, including support to the general public and explanation of dissemination-related processes and results. The relevant aspect is operational enquiry handling and provision of information about systems, processes, and program results. The subprocess needs capability to respond to enquiries, explain procedures, support standardized workflows, and produce manuals and training materials that can reduce repeated support burden. This position satisfies that need because it 'Responds orally and in writing to enquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information on the operation of divisional systems and processes and the use of program results.' It also 'Writes survey information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports,' which aligns with the subprocess emphasis on reusable knowledge assets and FAQ-style support content. The role further supports secure and compliant handling through contextual knowledge of 'the Statistics Act' and 'particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data.' While the role is more focused on collection and processing operations than dissemination support specifically, its enquiry-response, explanatory, and documentation responsibilities make it relevant at a medium level.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is implicated because subprocess 7.5 requires providing assistance to users and explaining outputs, concepts, methods, and limitations, especially where users need help understanding changing data sources, comparability, and quality. The relevant aspect is substantive support to users of statistical products. The subprocess needs capability to provide data assistance, explain technical concepts in accessible language, and assess how methodological or source changes affect products and services. This position satisfies that need because one key activity is 'Provides data and assistance to users, within and outside Statistics Canada.' It also 'Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional systems and applications.' This directly supports user support needs for interpretation and clarification. The role is also relevant to drivers concerning administrative and alternative data and metadata/discoverability because it 'Analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services' and 'Assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored.' Privacy and secure access considerations are also present through required awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts. Relevance is medium because user support is present but not the dominant focus of the role.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is relevant because subprocess 7.5 increasingly depends on support staff who can guide users on data use, governance, quality, and responsible access, especially under drivers such as AI/automation, administrative data, and privacy/security. The relevant aspect is advisory support to data users and clients, including explanation of governance and data quality issues that often arise in support requests. The subprocess needs capability to communicate clearly with users, understand data life cycle and quality, and protect sensitive information while supporting access and interpretation. This position satisfies that need because it 'Provides advice, information and guidance to data users and clients regarding governance concepts used to protect and optimize the utility of Statistics Canada’s data assets.' It also requires writing clear reports and presentations for 'managers and clients with varying levels of knowledge and understanding of data science' and includes data literacy skills to 'assess the quality of data, protect and secure data, and safeguard their responsible use.' These responsibilities align with support for user understanding, privacy-aware handling, and explanation of data limitations. The role is less directly tied to dissemination service operations than dedicated dissemination positions, so relevance is medium rather than high.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role has a limited but material connection to subprocess 7.5 because the subprocess includes reviewing user queries and requests as input to overarching quality management and identifying changing user needs. The relevant aspect is gathering and analyzing client requirements and feedback. The subprocess needs capability to assess information needs, synthesize qualitative and quantitative evidence, and communicate findings that can improve support services. This position satisfies that need through activities such as 'Provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data; gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases' and communication responsibilities requiring discussion of 'data requirements with Statistics Canada clients and evaluation colleagues.' It also participates in interviews and focus groups and undertakes research and analysis to identify useful data sources. However, the role is oriented to evaluation studies rather than operational dissemination support or direct handling of user service requests, so its connection is indirect and therefore low.
