implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is directly aligned to subprocess 8.1 because the subprocess is about identifying, gathering and compiling inputs used for evaluation, including qualitative and quantitative evidence, user feedback, staff suggestions, progress reports and specific follow-up studies. The role explicitly 'undertakes assigned tasks related to specific elements of evaluation projects such as, conducting literature and data research, identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data; participating in the conduct of interviews, and focus groups'. That is a direct match to gathering evaluation inputs from multiple sources. The subprocess also notes that evaluation inputs may include specific surveys or studies; this role supports that need through 'participating in the conduct of interviews, and focus groups' and through knowledge of 'research, including social science research and analysis' and 'program evaluation and performance measurement theories, processes and practices'. The drivers increase the volume and diversity of evaluation evidence, including operational metrics, cost indicators, staff feedback and methodological performance evidence. This role satisfies that need by 'provid[ing] support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data; gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases; and participates in the conduct of socio-economic analyses and cost-benefit analysis of programs' and by recommending 'enhancements to methods for retrieving data'. Communication requirements also support collecting inputs from clients and stakeholders, as the role must 'discuss data requirements with Statistics Canada clients and evaluation colleagues' and communicate with 'outside professionals to obtain data related to Statistics Canada and external evaluation studies'.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is materially connected because subprocess 8.1 explicitly includes process metadata, paradata, quality indicators and continuously captured evidence as core evaluation inputs. The work description is centered on producing, validating and evaluating metadata and metadata quality, which is especially relevant under the drivers for metadata standards, integrated pipelines, automation and cloud monitoring. The role 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository' and 'assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations and provides input to reports for clients and management'. That directly supports gathering and compiling metadata-based evaluation inputs and making them available for evaluation. The subprocess also requires quality indicators; this role provides that through 'evaluates selected indicators of statistical metadata quality across survey and statistical programs in accordance with pre-defined quality guidelines'. The capability needed is understanding metadata frameworks, standards compliance, interoperability and metadata quality evidence. The work description explicitly requires 'knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks' and 'knowledge of methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata'. It also supports transformation-related evidence gathering by analyzing 'current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives' and by participating in testing of new procedures and systems.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is strongly implicated because subprocess 8.1 increasingly depends on automated capture, preparation and assessment of diverse evaluation inputs such as system metrics, process logs, quality indicators, source information and operational data. The drivers for AI and automation, integrated pipelines, cloud infrastructure, open-source tools and operational efficiency all point to a need for data handling and analytical capability. The role supports this through 'conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin' and 'organizes and consolidates information relevant to the defined objectives of studies'. Those activities are directly relevant to compiling evaluation inputs from multiple operational and analytical sources. The capability needed is data lifecycle knowledge, quality assessment, standards conformance and secure handling of data. The work description explicitly includes 'knowledge of data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing... reporting, visualization, business intelligence' and 'knowledge of techniques and methods of information collection and analysis... in order to assess the quality of data and identify and mitigate risks to its integrity'. It also references data stewardship and security: 'Data literacy includes data stewardship and the ability to assess the quality of data, protect and secure data, and safeguard their responsible use.' This is materially relevant to gathering robust evaluation evidence from modern automated environments.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is directly relevant because subprocess 8.1 includes gathering operational evidence such as process metadata, paradata, system metrics, staff suggestions, collection results and reports on how processes performed. The Operations Officer works in the operational environment where such evidence is generated and assessed. The role 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data' and 'evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives'. That aligns closely with gathering evaluation inputs about operational performance and process effectiveness. The drivers for automation, orchestration, cloud monitoring, efficiency and workforce transformation increase the importance of operational logs, monitoring procedures, productivity indicators and pain points. This role satisfies that need by 'writ[ing] survey information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports' and by preparing 'reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems'. It also produces evidence specifically suited to evaluation, as it 'analyses reported data and work results and prepares reports for program managers or subject matter specialists, presenting findings on how the survey was conducted, problems encountered... and recommending alternatives'. The role's contextual knowledge of 'systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows' and awareness of privacy and confidentiality also support evaluation inputs related to secure and auditable operations.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because subprocess 8.1 requires gathering evidence on how statistical programs and methods are performing, including feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods. The work description explicitly states that the role 'participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities'. That is relevant to evaluation input gathering, especially under drivers related to methodological innovation and operational efficiency. The capability needed is the ability to assess impacts of methodological and procedural changes and to interpret data in context. The work description provides this through 'knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs' and through research activities that 'analyze changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services'. It is less directly focused on gathering evaluation inputs than the evaluation, metadata or operations roles, but it materially contributes evidence and analytical feedback used in evaluation.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is relevant because subprocess 8.1 includes compiling quality indicators and evidence from across the production lifecycle, and dissemination-stage evidence can inform evaluation of outputs, systems and user needs. The role 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases' and 'compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output... analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness'. Those activities support the need to gather quality-related evaluation inputs. The drivers for integrated pipelines, automation, administrative data and operational efficiency increase the need to assess effects of system and process changes on outputs and services. This role addresses that by 'analyz[ing] changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services' and by examining 'new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems'. It is not an evaluation-specific role, but it contributes materially to the collection of output quality and system-change evidence used in evaluation.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is directly aligned to subprocess 8.2 because the subprocess is about analyzing evaluation inputs, comparing results to expectations, synthesizing findings into reports or dashboards, identifying quality and performance issues, and recommending changes. The position's core responsibility is to participate in evaluation studies of programs, policies and initiatives 'to evaluate their relevance and performance.' It requires capability in gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data, applying analytical tools, determining implications of evaluation results, and formulating conclusions. It also supports assessment of data requirements, socio-economic and cost-benefit analysis, and provides supporting data for reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda for senior management. These responsibilities satisfy the subprocess need for evidence-based evaluation, benchmarking against expected performance, continuous improvement recommendations, and reporting. Evidence includes: 'conduct of evaluation studies related to programs, policies and initiatives, to evaluate their relevance and performance'; 'identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data'; 'applying analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of evaluation results and formulating conclusions'; 'participates in the conduct of socio-economic analyses and cost-benefit analysis'; and 'provides the Evaluation Manager with supporting data for sections of reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda.' The role is also materially connected to drivers such as AI and Automation, Modern Statistical Methods, Operational Efficiency and Cost Discipline, and Governance because it explicitly evaluates performance, methods, data use and costs.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because subprocess 8.2 must evaluate whether metadata, standards and discoverability objectives were achieved, especially under the metadata-related driver. The relevant subprocess aspect is evaluation of quality issues, process performance and recommendations for improvement, specifically where metadata quality, machine-readability, reuse and dissemination effectiveness are part of the evaluation inputs. The capability needed is to assess metadata quality, analyze metadata methods and systems, interpret requirements, and contribute to reports used by clients and management. This work description satisfies that need because it 'assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations,' 'provides input to reports for clients and management,' and 'analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives.' It also includes knowledge of 'statistical metadata concepts and frameworks' and of methods and systems used for 'producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata.' This is materially relevant to drivers on Metadata, Data Standards and Discoverability, Integrated Data Pipelines, Digital Platforms, and Cyber Security/Privacy because the role also requires awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts and evaluates metadata processes across programs.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because subprocess 8.2 increasingly depends on continuous monitoring, dashboarding, data quality assessment, and analysis of process performance under drivers such as AI and Automation, Integrated Data Pipelines, Digital Platforms, and Operational Efficiency. The relevant subprocess aspect is analyzing evaluation inputs, monitoring quality and performance metrics, and supporting dashboards or evidence for improvement decisions. The capability needed is data preparation, validation, quality assessment, analytical reporting, visualization and understanding of the data science lifecycle. This work description satisfies that need through responsibilities to 'conduct data preparation techniques' including 'data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin,' and through knowledge of 'reporting, visualization, business intelligence' and the ability to 'develop briefings, presentations and dashboards that contain valid and reliable data.' It also requires knowledge of data risk assessment, governance, protecting and securing data, and communicating analytical results to managers and clients. While not an evaluation-specialist role, it materially supports the evidence generation and monitoring capabilities needed for modern evaluation.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because subprocess 8.2 includes evaluating selected activities during execution, identifying operational quality issues, comparing performance to expected values, and recommending changes. The relevant subprocess aspect is operational evaluation of collection, coding and processing methods, procedures and results. The capability needed is to assess operational methods, analyze impacts of changes to data sources and outputs, prepare management reports, and recommend alternatives for improved efficiency and quality. This work description satisfies that need because it explicitly 'evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives,' and 'analyses reported data and work results and prepares reports for program managers or subject matter specialists, presenting findings on how the survey was conducted, problems encountered ... and recommending alternatives.' It also includes knowledge of management and control of statistical collection, coding and processing activities, verification methods to ensure reliability and consistency, and awareness of security and confidentiality obligations. This makes it materially relevant to drivers on process orchestration, operational efficiency, governance discipline, administrative data changes, and privacy/security controls.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because subprocess 8.2 requires analysis of outputs, assessment of methodological and procedural changes, identification of deviations or issues, and recommendations for future improvements. The relevant subprocess aspect is evaluating whether collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods remain relevant and effective. The capability needed is subject-matter analysis, assessment of trends and issues, evaluation of methodological impacts, and feedback on survey methods and activities. This work description satisfies that need because it 'participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.' It also includes research responsibilities to 'analyze changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services' and to 'analyze current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.' This is materially connected to drivers such as Modern Statistical Methods, Administrative and Alternative Data, Operational Efficiency, and Governance.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This role is implicated because subprocess 8.2 includes evaluating data quality, effects of system and methodological changes, and whether outputs and services meet expected standards. The relevant subprocess aspect is assessing quality issues and performance deviations in produced and disseminated statistical outputs, then informing recommendations for change. The capability needed is to review data quality from systems and databases, analyze consistency and reliability, assess impacts of procedural and technological changes, and communicate findings. This work description satisfies that need because it 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases,' 'analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness,' and 'analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.' It also examines 'new or revised processing specifications' to determine effects on integration and coordination with other systems. These responsibilities are materially relevant to drivers involving integrated pipelines, digital platforms, methodological innovation, metadata/standards dependencies, and operational efficiency.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is directly connected to agreeing an action plan because the subprocess is based on evaluation findings and requires decision-ready synthesis, reporting and discussion with management. The relevant aspect of the subprocess is turning evaluation evidence into agreed improvement actions and monitoring considerations. The needed capability is evaluation analysis, interpretation of findings, preparation of briefing material for senior management, and participation in discussions on evaluation requirements. This position satisfies that need because it 'participates as a member of project teams in the conduct of evaluation studies', applies analytical tools 'to determine implications of evaluation results and formulating conclusions', and 'provides the Evaluation Manager with supporting data for sections of reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda for senior management'. It also supports future-oriented planning through assessment of 'current and future requirements for data' and has knowledge of 'program evaluation and performance measurement theories, processes and practices'. These responsibilities materially support governance, prioritization, workforce adaptation, efficiency decisions, and monitored follow-through arising from evaluation.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is implicated because action plans under this subprocess may include remediation or enhancement of metadata quality, standards adoption, documentation, and discoverability, especially under the metadata and standards driver. The relevant aspect of the subprocess is agreeing concrete actions where evaluation findings identify metadata weaknesses or opportunities for standardization and improved quality monitoring. The needed capability is assessing metadata quality, analyzing impacts of procedural or system changes, advising clients on standards and policies, and contributing to reports and training. This position satisfies that need because it 'assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations and provides input to reports for clients and management', 'provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata', and 'analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives'. It also liaises with specialists and management 'to negotiate procedural modifications, priorities and target dates', which aligns with agreeing and implementing action plans.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is materially connected because many action plans influenced by AI and automation, integrated pipelines, governance, and workforce transformation depend on analytical evidence about data quality, risks, standards, and operational conditions. The relevant aspect of the subprocess is prioritizing and monitoring improvement actions related to data processes, automation, governance, and responsible use. The needed capability is data analysis, assessment of data quality and integrity, communication of findings to managers, and advice on governance concepts. This position satisfies that need because it conducts 'data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin', provides 'advice, information and guidance to data users and clients regarding governance concepts used to protect and optimize the utility of Statistics Canada’s data assets', and prepares 'analytical reports, briefings and presentation material'. Its knowledge includes the data science life cycle, data stewardship, protecting and securing data, and assessing risks to integrity, all of which support action planning for modernization and monitored improvement.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is strongly implicated because agreeing an action plan often requires operational recommendations on collection, coding, processing, workflow efficiency, controls, training, and privacy/security remediation. The relevant aspect of the subprocess is deciding and documenting operational improvement actions and mechanisms for monitoring implementation impacts. The needed capability is evaluation of operational methods and results, recommendation of alternatives, preparation of reports outlining options and requirements, and coordination with specialists and stakeholders. This position satisfies that need because it 'evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives', 'prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems', and 'analyses reported data and work results and prepares reports for program managers or subject matter specialists... recommending alternatives'. It also writes 'monitoring procedures and management reports' and has explicit awareness of the 'Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data', which is relevant to action plans driven by efficiency, governance, and secure access.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is implicated because the subprocess requires translating analytical and methodological findings into agreed changes to survey methods, procedures, priorities, and project plans. The relevant aspect of the subprocess is using evaluation evidence to establish improvement actions, procedural modifications, and target dates for future cycles. The needed capability is analysis of program data and methods, assessment of impacts of methodological and technological changes, and liaison to establish plans and priorities. This position satisfies that need because it 'participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities'. It also liaises with others 'to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates'. Its research responsibilities include analyzing changes in 'procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services' and proposing alternative systems, which aligns with action planning under modernization and execution-discipline drivers.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This work description is materially connected because evaluation-based action plans may include changes to data production, dissemination, system integration, user service, training, and quality controls. The relevant aspect of the subprocess is agreeing practical actions to improve outputs, products, services, and dissemination processes in response to evaluation findings. The needed capability is assessing impacts of procedural and system changes, interpreting user requirements, analyzing data quality and operational effects, and contributing to training and documentation. This position satisfies that need because it 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases', 'analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services', and 'examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems'. It also drafts reports and training materials and liaises with specialists to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, supporting implementation of agreed actions.
